question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to enable its sales team with automatic post-call visibility into mention of competitors, products, and other custom phrases. Which feature should the Agentforce Specialist set up to enable UC's sales team?
optionA: Call Summaries
optionB: Call Explorer
optionC: Call Insights
explanation:
Call Insights is the feature to set up. Einstein Conversation Insights records and analyses voice and video calls for mentions of specific keywords and phrases, and Call Insights is the part that surfaces them: mentions of competitors, products, pricing, next steps, and the custom keywords you define during setup. That gives the sales team automatic post-call visibility without anyone listening back through the recording.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Call Summaries) — condenses what happened on a call rather than tracking defined mentions across calls.
Option B (Call Explorer) — a search interface for asking questions about call content; it does not deliver the standing competitor-and-product signal this team asked for.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.call_coaching.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.call_coaching_setup_insights.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Service Agent at Universal Containers (UC) is designed to help customers resolve issues by searching against knowledge articles. Knowledge articles have PDF attachments that add critical details. UC reports that the agent provides excellent summaries of the knowledge articles, but seems completely unaware of the PDF attachments. How should an Agentforce Specialist configure the Data Cloud search index to include the content of these attached files?
optionA: Increase article chunk size and token limits for Knowledge indexing so larger contexts capture attachment references.
optionB: Enable 'Include Related Attachments' for Knowledge-- kav and map the ContentDocumentLink unstructured data model object (UDMO).
optionC: Use Data Cloud's 'Include Attachments' option and select the ContentDocumentVersion unstructured data model object (UDMO).
explanation:
Using Data Cloud's 'Include Attachments' option and selecting the ContentDocumentVersion unstructured data model object is the configuration, because the text of an attached file does not live on the article, and it does not live on the link record either. When Data 360 ingests file attachments from CRM objects it deploys three content data streams: Content Document (the document), Content Version (the specific version of the document, which carries the file content), and Content Document Link (the link to the records the file is shared with). You then create a search index to enable file attachment ingestion, and Data 360 converts that content into searchable vectors, which is what puts PDF text within reach of the agent's retrieval.
One thing to know about scale: the initial ingestion covers up to 100,000 of the most recent historical files per CRM object, and new attachments are ingested incrementally after that.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (increase chunk size and token limits for Knowledge indexing) — changes how article text is split; it cannot index a file that was never ingested.
Option B (map the ContentDocumentLink UDMO) — the link object records only what the file is attached to, not the file's content; the index has to point at the version object.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_unstructured_data_connect_content_document.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: In addition to Recipient and Sender, which object should an Agentforce utilize for inserting merge fields into a Sales email template prompt?
optionA: Recipient Opportunities
optionB: Recipient Account
optionC: User Organization
explanation:
The Recipient Account is the third object. A sales email prompt template is scoped by who it is written to and what it may draw on: you choose a Recipient type (the lead, contact, or person account the email addresses) and then, optionally, select an Object to include data from a related object, such as Account, in the generated email. Sender covers the rep's own details, so the account behind the recipient is the third source of merge fields. The template's related-object slot takes one related object for context, and the account is the documented example.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Recipient Opportunities) — the related-object slot takes a single related object, and the documented one is the account, not the recipient's opportunity list.
Option C (User Organization) — nothing in the template pulls from a user's organisation record.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_create_sales_email_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.prompt_builder_add_merge_fields_sales_email.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers' service team wants to customize the standard case summary response from Agentforce. What should the Agentforce Specialist do to achieve this?
optionA: Create a custom Record Summary prompt template for the Case object.
optionB: Summarize the Case with a standard Agent action.
optionC: Customize the standard Record Summary template for the Case object.
explanation:
Creating a custom Record Summary prompt template for the Case object is what customising the standard summary means, because you do not edit a standard prompt template in place. Salesforce's mechanism is an override: overridable standard templates are flagged in the Category column, you create a new version with Save As, and when you activate that custom version it takes the place of the standard one; only one version is active at a time.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (summarize the Case with a standard Agent action) — changes nothing about the wording the summary comes out with; the action is what runs, the template is what shapes the response.
Option C (customize the standard Record Summary template) — standard templates cannot be edited directly; the supported route is a custom version that overrides the standard one.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_override_standard_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Salesforce Administrator is exploring the capabilities of Agent to enhance user interaction within their organization. They are particularly interested in how Agent processes user requests and the mechanism it employs to deliver responses. The administrator is evaluating whether Agent directly interfaces with a large language model (LLM) to fetch and display responses to user inquiries, facilitating a broad range of requests from users. How does Agent handle user requests In Salesforce?
optionA: Agent will trigger a flow that utilizes a prompt template to generate the message.
optionB: Agent will perform an HTTP callout to an LLM provider.
optionC: Agent analyzes the user's request and LLM technology is used to generate and display the appropriate response.
explanation:
Agent analyzes the user's request and LLM technology is used to generate and display the appropriate response; Agentforce is not a thin wrapper over a model endpoint. Salesforce describes the reasoning engine as a series of carefully orchestrated prompts sent to an LLM: the agent classifies the user's message into the best-matching subagent, then decides its next step (running an action, asking for more information, or answering directly), with each step representing one or more LLM calls. The model supplies the language; the platform decides what to ask it and what to do with the answer.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Agent triggers a flow that uses a prompt template) — a flow can be one of the actions an agent runs, but an agent is not simply a flow that invokes a prompt template.
Option B (Agent performs an HTTP callout to an LLM provider) — the agent does not make a raw HTTP callout to an LLM provider from the org; the platform's reasoning engine and Trust Layer sit between the agent and the model.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_reasoning_engine.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers, dealing with a high volume of chat inquiries, implements Einstein Work Summaries to boost productivity. After an agent-customer conversation, which additional information does Einstein generate and fill, apart from the "summary"?
optionA: Sentiment Analysis and Emotion Detection
optionB: Draft Survey Request Email
optionC: Issue and Revolution
explanation:
Issue and Resolution are the additional fields, because Einstein Work Summaries fills three things, not one. At the end of a conversation between a rep and a customer, or with a single click from the Case page, Einstein predicts and fills a summary, an issue, and a resolution, which the rep can then review, edit, and save.
Note that the keyed option is misspelled in this item: it reads 'Revolution' where the documented field is Resolution.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Sentiment Analysis and Emotion Detection) — a different capability, not what Work Summaries writes.
Option B (Draft Survey Request Email) — not part of the feature at all.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.cc_generative_ai_work_summaries.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has configured a data library and wants to restrict indexing of knowledge articles to articles which are only publicly available in their knowledge base, UC also wants the agent to link sources that the large language model (LLM) grounded its response on. Which settings should help UC with this?
optionA: In the data library setting window, under Knowledge Settings, enable Use Public Knowledge Article and select Show sources,
optionB: In the data library setting window, under Knowledge Settings, enable Use Public Knowledge Article. It is not possible to display articles that the LLM grounded its response in.
optionC: Use Data Categories to categorize publicly available articles to index. Sources are automatically displayed when knowledge articles are categorized as Public.
explanation:
Enabling Use Public Knowledge Article and selecting Show sources in the data library's Knowledge Settings covers both halves of the requirement, and both settings exist. Restricting what gets indexed is done in the library's Knowledge settings, and citations are a separate switch: Salesforce's instruction is that to include citations in the agent's output you select Show Sources, and then add your Salesforce Knowledge domain URL so responses link back to the article they were grounded on. If you do not supply a domain URL, the publicly available URL is used.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Use Public Knowledge Article, but sources cannot be displayed) — directly disproved by the Show Sources setting, which exists to display the articles the LLM grounded on.
Option C (Data Categories with sources shown automatically for Public articles) — data categories organise articles for visibility and search; categorising articles as public does not cause sources to be displayed, because displaying sources is the Show Sources setting.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_select_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_data_sources.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Choose 1 option. How does Agentforce select the correct action to resolve a user's request?
optionA: Each topic contains a list of the matching action's user utterances so that the agent can map the user request to the right topic and action.
optionB: The large language model (LLM) selects the right topic and action, if they exist. If there are no matches, the LLM attempts to answer the user's request.
optionC: The reasoning engine identifies the agent action to be executed by its name and action input instructions.
explanation:
The large language model selects the right topic and action if they exist, and attempts to answer the request when there is no match, because selection is a model decision, not a lookup. Salesforce documents the path of a user message as iterative classification and reasoning: the agent classifies the message into the best-matching subagent, then decides what to do (run one or more actions, ask the user for more information, ask a clarifying question, or respond directly to the request). Each of those steps is one or more LLM calls.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (each topic contains a list of matching user utterances) — there is no stored list of utterances per topic that the agent matches against; classification is done by the model from the topic's description and instructions.
Option C (the reasoning engine identifies the action by its name and input instructions) — the action's name and instructions inform the model's choice rather than replacing it; the engine does not resolve an action from its name alone.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_reasoning_engine.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_instructions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Service Agent, who has been successfully assisting customers with service requests in Salesforce, is now unable to help customers with issues related to a new product replacement process. The company recently implemented a custom Product Replacement object in Salesforce to track and manage these replacements. Which Agentforce Agent User change must be implemented to address this issue?
optionA: The permission set group assigned to the Agent User needs to grant access to the Product Replacement flow.
optionB: The permission set assigned to the Agent User needs Read access to the custom Product Replacement object.
optionC: The profile assigned to the Agentforce Agent User needs AI training permission to the custom Product Replacement object.
explanation:
The permission set assigned to the Agent User needs Read access to the custom Product Replacement object, because an agent sees what its user can see. The agent user is created with minimal access so the agent is secure by default, and you expand that access deliberately, based on the principle of least privilege, so a brand-new custom object is invisible to the agent until the agent user is granted Read on it through its permission set.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (permission set group granting access to the Product Replacement flow) — access to a flow is granted by the Run Flows permission or per-flow access, and it governs whether the agent can execute automation, not whether it can read Product Replacement records.
Option C (AI training permission on the object) — no such permission exists; agents ground on data they are permitted to read, they are not trained on objects.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_user.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_actions_common_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A Salesforce Agentforce Specialist is reviewing the feedback from a customer about the ineffectiveness of the prompt template. What should the Agentforce Specialist do to ensure the prompt template's effectiveness?
optionA: Monitor and refine the template based on user feedback.
optionB: Use the Prompt Builder Scorecard to help monitor.
optionC: Periodically change the templates grounding object.
explanation:
Monitoring and refining the template based on user feedback is what Salesforce documents for an ineffective template: iteration against real feedback. You revise the template and generate a new output (the previous output is not saved and the new one replaces it), and the best practices say plainly to iterate on your prompt templates, trying the same goal different ways, and to get end-user feedback to see how well the template generates the desired response.
The closest thing to a metrics surface is Prompt Performance Metrics in Prompt Builder, still in beta, which reports template usage from Data 360. That is a usage signal, not a scorecard that grades a template, and it does not replace the review-and-revise loop.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Prompt Builder Scorecard) — there is no Prompt Builder Scorecard; the feature does not exist.
Option C (periodically change the template's grounding object) — the grounding object is what supplies the record context; swapping it changes what the template is about rather than making it more effective.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.prompt_builder_review_revise.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_enable_prompt_performance_metrics.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: B->A. The Prompt Builder Scorecard named by the original key does not exist in Prompt Builder — a scorecard is an Einstein Prediction Builder feature. Salesforce documents monitoring and refining a template through the review-and-revise loop and end-user feedback, with Prompt Performance Metrics (Beta) as the only reporting surface, so A is the supported answer.

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to create a new Sales Email prompt template in Prompt Builder using the "Save As" function. However, UC notices that the new template produces different results compared to the standard Sales Email prompt due to missing hyperparameters. What should UC do to ensure the new prompt template produces results comparable to the standard Sales Email prompts?
optionA: Use Model Playground to create a model configuration with the specified parameters.
optionB: Manually add the hyperparameters to the new template.
optionC: Revert to using the standard template without modifications.
explanation:
Using Model Playground to create a model configuration with the specified parameters is the documented fix for a documented gap, and the fix is not in the template. Salesforce states that standard sales email prompts use hard-coded hyperparameters that are not copied when you use Save As, which is why a copied template produces different or unexpected results. The remedy it gives is to use AI Models (formerly Einstein Studio) to create a model configuration with specific parameters (model gpt-3.5-turbo, temperature 1.0, frequencyPenalty 1.0, presencePenalty 0.5), which you build and evaluate in Model Playground.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (manually add the hyperparameters to the new template) — hyperparameters are set on a model configuration, not typed into the prompt template; there is no field in the template body where they live.
Option C (revert to the standard template) — abandons the customisation UC wanted rather than solving anything.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_prompt_templates.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_foundation_models.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: B->A. Salesforce documents that the standard sales email hyperparameters are hard-coded and not copied by Save As, and directs you to create a model configuration in AI Models (formerly Einstein Studio) with the listed parameters. Hyperparameters are not something you add manually to the prompt template, so the original key described a step that does not exist.

question: Universal Containers (UC) is experimenting with using public Generative AI models and is familiar with the language required to get the information it needs. However, it can be time-consuming for both UC's sales and service reps to type in the prompt to get the information they need, and ensure prompt consistency. Which Salesforce feature should the company use to address these concerns?
optionA: Agent Builder and Action: Query Records.
optionB: Einstein Prompt Builder and Prompt Templates.
optionC: Einstein Recommendation Builder.
explanation:
Einstein Prompt Builder and Prompt Templates address both concerns. The problem described is repetition and inconsistency in how people phrase prompts, which is exactly what a prompt template removes: Prompt Builder lets you write the prompt once, ground it in CRM data with merge fields, and hand users a button instead of a blank box, so the wording is authored once and applied the same way every time.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Agent Builder and the Query Records action) — puts a conversational layer in front of data retrieval rather than standardising a prompt.
Option C (Einstein Recommendation Builder) — produces predictive recommendations rather than generated text.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_template_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers' Agent Action includes several Apex classes for the new Agentforce Agent. What is an important consideration when deploying Apex that is invoked by an Agent Action?
optionA: The Apex classes must have at least 75% code coverage from unit tests, and all dependencies must be in the deployment package.
optionB: Apex classes invoked by an Agent Action may be deployed with less than 75% test coverage as long as the agent is not activated in production.
optionC: The Apex classes may bypass the 75% code coverage requirement as long as they are only used by the agent.
explanation:
That the Apex classes must have at least 75% code coverage from unit tests, with all dependencies in the deployment package, is the consideration, because Apex behind an agent action is ordinary Apex and carries the platform's ordinary deployment rules: to deploy Apex, unit tests must cover at least 75% of your Apex code and those tests must pass. Nothing about being invoked by an agent relaxes that, and the deployment package still has to contain the classes the action depends on or the deployment fails on the missing dependency.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (less than 75% coverage while the agent is not activated) — coverage is checked when the code is deployed, not when an agent is activated, so leaving the agent inactive changes nothing.
Option C (bypass the requirement when used only by the agent) — there is no agent-only carve-out from the coverage requirement.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_code_coverage_intro.htm

question: What is a Salesforce Agentforce Specialist able to configure in Data Masking within the Einstein Trust Layer?
optionA: The profiles exempt from masking
optionB: The encryption keys for masking
optionC: The privacy data entities to be masked
explanation:
The privacy data entities to be masked are what a Specialist configures. Data masking in the Einstein Trust Layer is configured by choosing what counts as sensitive: on the Data Masking tab of Einstein Trust Layer setup, masking is on by default and individual privacy data entities or whole categories can be turned on or off, taking effect within a few minutes. The Trust Layer detects that data, replaces it with placeholder text before the prompt leaves for the model, and keeps the mapping so the response can be demasked on the way back.
One current caveat worth knowing: data masking for LLMs is disabled for agents. It applies to embedded generative AI features such as Einstein Service Replies and Einstein Work Summaries, which is where you configure it.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the profiles exempt from masking) — there is no per-profile exemption list for masking.
Option B (the encryption keys for masking) — the encryption keys used to protect data are not part of this configuration; masking substitutes placeholders, it does not encrypt.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.generative_ai_trust_setup.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question:
Universal Containers (UC) wants to build an Agentforce Service Agent that provides the latest, active, and relevant policy and compliance information to customers. The agent must:
Semantically search HR policies, compliance guidelines, and company procedures.
Ensure responses are grounded on published Knowledge.
Allow Knowledge updates to be reflected immediately without manual reconfiguration.
What should UC do to ensure the agent retrieves the right information?
optionA: Enable the agent to search all internal records and past customer inquiries.
optionB: Set up an Agentforce Data Library to store and index policy documents for AI retrieval.
optionC: Manually add policy responses into the AI model to prevent hallucinations.
explanation:
Setting up an Agentforce Data Library to store and index policy documents for AI retrieval is what all three requirements point at. A library indexes your knowledge articles and fields, file uploads, or web sources so agents know what to base responses on, and creating one automatically pushes data streams to Data 360, maps the objects, and builds a search index and retriever. Retrieval over that index is semantic rather than keyword, which is what 'semantically search HR policies' asks for, and the agent grounds on it through the Answer Questions with Knowledge action.
The immediacy requirement is handled by the same machinery: the index picks up new and modified records incrementally after the initial build, so published Knowledge updates flow through without reconfiguring the agent.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (search all internal records and past customer inquiries) — widens the surface to unvetted content instead of published policy.
Option C (manually add policy responses into the AI model) — there is no mechanism for adding responses 'into the AI model'; you ground a model, you do not load answers into it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_concept.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_data_sources.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What should an Agentforce consider when using related list merge fields in a prompt template associated with an Account object in Prompt Builder?
optionA: The Activities related list on the Account object is not supported because it is a polymorphic field.
optionB: If person accounts have been enabled, merge fields will not be available for the Account object.
optionC: Prompt generation will yield no response when there is no related list associated with an Account in runtime.
explanation:
That the Activities related list on the Account object is not supported is the consideration. Salesforce states the limitation directly in its considerations for grounding with related lists: Activities related lists on objects such as Account and Case are not supported. So an Account prompt template cannot pull the activity history through a related list merge field, however natural that would be for a summary.
Two related rules from the same page are worth carrying with it. Only related lists present on the object's page layout are available for grounding, and the fields come from the parent object's layout for the current user. And if a user lacks the related list on their layout or Read permission on the associated object, no related list data is sent to the LLM; the prompt still runs.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (person accounts remove merge fields for Account) — person accounts do not remove merge field support for Account.
Option C (no response when there is no related list at runtime) — when related list data is unavailable the prompt still runs without it; it does not yield no response.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_related_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants an AI agent to answer questions about warranties using unstructured data stored in Data Cloud. Results must be filterable by product line and ranked by recent updates.
optionA: Use the default retriever which automatically accounts for recency ranking.
optionB: Build a custom retriever in Einstein Studio with product line filters and recency ranking.
optionC: Apply semantic embeddings with default metadata filters to achieve the desired result.
explanation:
Building a custom retriever in Einstein Studio with product line filters and recency ranking is the approach. A data library's default retriever answers general questions over the indexed content; it does not come with product-line filtering or recency ranking. When you need retrieval shaped that way, you build a custom retriever, which is also how you reach more Data 360 source types and ensemble configurations.
One limitation is worth knowing before designing around filters: dynamic pre-filters are not supported when a data library is used with the Answer Questions with Knowledge prompt template; only static pre-filters are. The documented workarounds are a separate library per category or brand, or a custom Apex invocable action that passes filter values at runtime.
Naming note: retrievers are configured in Data 360; Einstein Studio is the exam-era name for what is now AI Models.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (default retriever automatically accounts for recency ranking) — assuming the default retriever ranks by recency is exactly the assumption this question is testing; it does not.
Option C (semantic embeddings with default metadata filters) — not a configuration Salesforce exposes.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_custom_retriever.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_concept.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) needs to create a prompt template that provides a detailed product description based on the latest product data. The description will be used in marketing materials to ensure consistency and accuracy. Which prompt template type should UC use?
optionA: Sales Email
optionB: Field Generation
optionC: Record Summary
explanation:
Field Generation is the template type, because the output here is a field value that lives on the product record and gets reused downstream: generative AI-enabled fields let a user populate a record field with generated content in one click, and the template draws on the record's current data each time it runs.
Remember the prerequisite that comes with this template type: the field has to sit on a Lightning record page that uses Dynamic Forms before it can be enabled for generative AI.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Sales Email) — scoped to a recipient and an email body, not a durable description attached to the product.
Option C (Record Summary) — condenses a record for someone reading it rather than writing a description into a field.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sf.prompt_builder_add_field_gen_to_lightning_record_page.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_template_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question:
An Agentforce Specialist at Universal Containers (UC) is building with no-code tools only. They have many small accounts that are only touched periodically by a specialized sales team, and UC wants to maximize the sales operations team's time. UC wants to help prep the sales team for calls by:
Summarizing past purchases.
Displaying products the contact has shown interest in (with data captured via Data Cloud).
Providing a recap of past email and phone conversations that have transcripts.
Which approach should the Agentforce Specialist recommend to achieve this goal?
optionA: Deploy UC's own custom foundational model on this data first.
optionB: Fine-tune the standard foundational model due to the complexity of the data.
optionC: Use a prompt template grounded on CRM and Data Cloud data using standard foundation models.
explanation:
Using a prompt template grounded on CRM and Data Cloud data with standard foundation models is the approach, because everything this team needs is grounding, and grounding is a no-code configuration. A prompt template assembled in Prompt Builder can merge record fields, related lists, flows, Apex, and Data 360 DMOs into one prompt, which covers past purchases from CRM, interest signals captured in Data 360, and call and email transcripts, all against the standard foundation models, with the Trust Layer applying masking and retention policies on the way through.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (deploy UC's own custom foundational model) — a code-and-data-science project that is not necessary to make a model reason over data you can already supply as context, and not a no-code tool.
Option B (fine-tune the standard foundational model) — fine-tuning changes what a model knows in general; grounding changes what it is told about this account, which is what a call prep brief requires.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which feature in the Einstein Trust Layer helps to minimize the risks of jailbreaking and prompt injection attacks?
optionA: Secure Data Retrieval and Grounding
optionB: Data Masking
optionC: Prompt Defense
explanation:
Prompt Defense is the Trust Layer's named answer to this threat. Salesforce describes it as the system policies that Prompt Builder and the Prompt Template Connect API apply to decrease the likelihood of the LLM generating something unintended or harmful (instructions telling the model how to behave, such as not answering on content it has no information about) and states that system policies are one way to defend against jailbreaking and prompt injection attacks.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Secure Data Retrieval and Grounding) — controls which records may enter a prompt, enforcing the running user's permissions; it limits what an attacker could extract but is not aimed at an instruction that tries to talk the model out of its rules.
Option B (Data Masking) — replaces sensitive values with placeholders before the prompt leaves Salesforce; it protects data, not the model's instructions.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A business stakeholder wants to use Al to generate a summary based on Data Cloud data. Which method(s) should the stakeholder use to access Data Cloud data from Prompt Builder?
optionA: Accessing data model objects (DMQs) directly in Flex templates, using Data Cloud related lists, and fetching Data Cloud data using prompt-initiated flows
optionB: Using Data Cloud related lists and fetching Data Cloud data using prompt-initiated flows
optionC: Using only external APIs to import Data Cloud data into Prompt Builder
explanation:
Accessing data model objects directly in Flex templates, using Data Cloud related lists, and fetching Data Cloud data using prompt-initiated flows are all documented methods; Prompt Builder reaches Data 360 in more than two ways, and the third is direct. Salesforce lists what the Insert Resource button can reference in a prompt template: record fields, flows, Apex, Data 360 DMOs, and related lists. So a data model object can be merged into a template as a resource in its own right: after Data 360 enrichments create the relationship, the DMO appears under the Actions section of the Insert Resources menu and behaves like native Salesforce data. The other two routes are real as well: Data 360 enrichments surface DMO data as copy fields and related lists on Salesforce objects, and a template-triggered prompt flow can fetch Data 360 data and merge its output into the template's resolution.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (related lists and prompt-initiated flows only) — incomplete; it omits the direct DMO resource, which is a documented third route.
Option C (only external APIs) — nothing about this requires importing Data 360 data into Prompt Builder from outside, since the platform exposes it natively.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_dmo.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_prompt_template_capability.htm&language=en_US&type=5

The original key excluded direct DMO access, but Salesforce documents the Insert Resource button as referencing record fields, flows, Apex, Data 360 DMOs, and related lists — so DMOs are available in a template directly, alongside the related-list and prompt-flow routes the old key allowed.

question: How does an Agent respond when it can't understand the request or find any requested information?
optionA: With a preconfigured message, based on the action type.
optionB: With a general message asking the user to rephrase the request.
optionC: With a generated error message.
explanation:
A general message asking the user to rephrase the request is the response, and the documented path for it is deliberately generic. If the reasoning engine can't find an appropriate subagent for what the user said, the agent moves to an Off-Topic system subagent and tries to bring the conversation back to the subagents it does have, which the user experiences as a general message inviting them to restate the request, not as a failure.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a preconfigured message based on the action type) — messages are not preconfigured per action type; an action that is never selected produces no message of its own.
Option C (a generated error message) — an error message is a different thing entirely; system messages cover errors, and not understanding a request is not an error.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_reasoning_engine.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_setup_system_messages.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Choose 1 option. Before activating a custom agent action, an Agentforce Specialist would like to evaluate multiple real-world user utterances to ensure the action is being selected appropriately. Which tool should the Agentforce Specialist recommend?
optionA: Testing Center
optionB: AgentForce Builder
optionC: Prompt Builder
explanation:
Testing Center is the documented tool for evaluating many utterances before an action goes live. It supports large-scale batch testing from scenarios you upload as a CSV, and its evaluations cover subagent and action validation, which is precisely the question being asked here: whether the custom action is selected when it should be.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Agentforce Builder) — its Preview panel does show which subagents and actions an utterance selected and why, but it is one utterance at a time, so it cannot establish behaviour across many real-world phrasings.
Option C (Prompt Builder) — authors and tests prompt templates; it has no view of which agent action a request routes to.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_builder_tour.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The Agentforce Specialist for Coral Cloud Resorts wants to create an agent that will automate the resolution of a large portion of guest complaints related to their vacation experiences. The agent will be able to offer upgrades, hotel credit, and other complimentary options. The agent will also be in charge of escalating the case to a human when a guest has suffered a major disruption (such as cancellation). Following Salesforce best practices, which type of agent should the Agentforce Specialist create?
optionA: Sales A Agent with a Flex prompt template
optionB: Custom Agent with a Flex prompt template
optionC: Service Agent with a Flex prompt template
explanation:
A Service Agent with a Flex prompt template is the type to create. Salesforce's agent type table describes the Service Agent as intelligently supporting customers with common inquiries and escalating complex issues, which is this scenario exactly: resolve the routine complaints with credits and upgrades, hand the major disruptions to a human. It is also the type built for customer-facing channels, including an Experience Cloud site with built-in authentication.
The flex prompt template is the right partner for it because the offers being generated do not fit a standard template type; flex is documented as the type for any use case the others do not cover, with inputs you define.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Sales Agent with a Flex prompt template) — there is no Sales Agent template in the agent type table, and the sales-side agents work prospects rather than resolving guest complaints.
Option B (Custom Agent with a Flex prompt template) — 'custom agent' is not a type either; you customise one of the documented types rather than choosing a generic one.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_explore_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_create_flex_prompt_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers implemented Agentforce for its users. One user complains that an Agent is not deleting activities from the past 7 days. What is the reason for this issue?
optionA: Agentforce does not have the permission to delete the user's records.
optionB: Agentforce Delete Record Action permission is not associated to the user.
optionC: Agentforce does not have a standard Delete Record action.
explanation:
That Agentforce does not have a standard Delete Record action is the reason. The Standard Agent Action Reference has no general Delete Record action: it ships Create Record, Update Record, Get Record Details, Query Records and their relatives, and the only delete actions in the catalogue are vertical ones (Agentforce IT Service's Delete Configuration Item, Field Service's Delete Temporary Appointment), which are specific to those products. So the agent is not being blocked by a permission; it has no action that deletes records to select in the first place.
If deletion is genuinely required, it has to be built: an Apex or flow custom action that performs the delete, subject to the agent user's own permissions.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Agentforce lacks permission to delete the user's records) — granting the agent user delete access on the object would still leave the agent with nothing to call.
Option B (Agentforce Delete Record Action permission not associated to the user) — there is no such permission to assign.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_ref.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_custom.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to enable its sales team to use Al to suggest recommended products from its catalog. Which type of prompt template should UC use?
optionA: Record summary prompt template
optionB: Email generation prompt template
optionC: Flex prompt template
explanation:
A Flex prompt template is the type to use, because recommending products from a catalogue is not one of the shapes Salesforce ships a template for, and that is precisely when you reach for flex: it is documented as the type for any use case the other template types do not cover, and it is the one where you define the inputs yourself, up to five resources, each named and optionally required.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Record summary prompt template) — condenses one record for a reader; it is not a way to ask a model to select and justify products against a customer's context.
Option B (Email generation prompt template) — produces a message to a recipient, not a product recommendation.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_create_flex_prompt_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_template_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Support agents at Universal Containers are using Agentforce to find troubleshooting information. They've reported that the agent frequently provides knowledge articles that are outdated, even when newer versions of the articles are available. The administrator has confirmed that all articles are correctly chunked and indexed. Which configuration change in the Data Cloud hybrid search index best addresses this problem?
optionA: Disable the keyword index to rely solely on the vector index.
optionB: Switch the chunking strategy from section-aware to fixed-size.
optionC: Add a ranking factor for regency based on the LastModifiedDate field.
explanation:
Adding a ranking factor for recency based on the LastModifiedDate field is the configuration change, because when chunking and indexing are already correct, what is left is ranking. Data 360 hybrid search retrieves from a keyword index and a vector index, fuses the results, and then reranks them, and during setup you can configure additional ranking factors such as recency of records and popularity. Salesforce's own example is the one this question needs: use the LastModifiedDate field of an indexed DMO to define the recency of a record. (The option text misspells it 'regency'.)
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (disable the keyword index) — throws away half of hybrid search, which costs exact-match precision on error codes and part numbers without doing anything about age.
Option B (switch chunking from section-aware to fixed-size) — changes how articles are split, and cutting across section boundaries generally degrades the passages rather than favouring newer ones.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_hybridsearch_fusion_ranking.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) implements a custom retriever to improve the accuracy of AI-generated responses. UC notices that the retriever is returning too many irrelevant results, making the responses less useful. What should UC do to ensure only relevant data is retrieved?
optionA: Define filters to narrow the search results based on specific conditions.
optionB: Change the search index to a different data model object (DMO).
optionC: Increase the maximum number of results returned to capture a broader dataset.
explanation:
Defining filters to narrow the search results based on specific conditions is the fix, because too many irrelevant results is a scoping problem, and retrievers are scoped with filters. A custom retriever supports pre-filters that narrow what is eligible to be returned before ranking, so the results the model grounds on are drawn from the right slice of the index.
One limitation to design around: dynamic pre-filters are not supported when a data library is used with the Answer Questions with Knowledge prompt template; only static pre-filters are. The documented workarounds are a separate library per category or brand, or a custom Apex invocable action that passes filter values at runtime.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (change the search index to a different DMO) — changes what corpus is searched rather than tightening retrieval within the right corpus.
Option C (increase the maximum number of results) — does the opposite of what is needed; a broader dataset dilutes the context window with more of the same irrelevance.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_custom_retriever.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is rolling out a new generative AI initiative. Which Prompt Builder limitations should the Agentforce Specialist be aware of?
optionA: Rich text area fields are only supported in Flex template types.
optionB: Creations or updates to the prompt templates are not recorded in the Setup Audit Trail.
optionC: Custom objects are supported only for Flex template types.
explanation:
That creations or updates to prompt templates are not recorded in the Setup Audit Trail is the limitation. Salesforce lists it under Prompt Builder Limitations in as many words: audit trail isn't supported, and creating or updating a prompt template isn't tracked in the Setup Audit Trail. For a governance-minded rollout that is the limitation worth knowing, because template changes alter what the LLM is told without leaving the usual trace.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (rich text area fields only in Flex templates) — rich text area fields are not confined to flex templates.
Option C (custom objects only for Flex templates) — custom objects are not restricted to flex templates; the same page says only that a newly created custom object or field isn't available in Prompt Builder immediately, and logging out and back in makes it usable.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_limitations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: In the context of retriever and search indexes, what best describes the data preparation process in Data Cloud?
optionA: Data preparation focuses on real-time data ingestion and dynamic indexing to generate dynamic grounding reference data without preprocessing steps.
optionB: Data preparation entails aggregating, normalizing, and encoding structured datasets to ensure compliance with data governance and security protocols.
optionC: Data preparation Involves loading, chunking, vectorizing, and storing content in a search-optimized manner to support retrieval from the vector database.
explanation:
Loading, chunking, vectorizing, and storing content in a search-optimized manner to support retrieval from the vector database is how Salesforce describes the pipeline, in the same terms the option uses. The chunks are embedded by a supported model (E5-large-v2 and Multilingual-E5-large at 512 tokens, SFR-v2-small at 8,000) and stored in an index a retriever can query for the passages most similar to a question.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (real-time ingestion and dynamic indexing without preprocessing) — dynamic grounding at run time still depends on content having been chunked and vectorised in advance.
Option B (aggregating, normalizing, and encoding structured datasets for governance) — describes a data modelling exercise, not the preparation behind vector retrieval.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_search_index_ground_ai.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_search_index_reference.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) currently tracks Leads with a custom object. UC is preparing to implement the Sales Development Representative (SDR) Agent. Which consideration should UC keep in mind?
optionA: Agentforce SDR only works with the standard Lead object.
optionB: Agentforce SDR only works on Opportunities.
optionC: Agentforce SDR only supports custom objects associated with Accounts.
explanation:
That Agentforce SDR only works with the standard Lead object is the consideration: the agent works against Salesforce's standard prospect records, not a custom object. Prospects are assigned to a Lead Nurturing agent from the lead, contact, or person account detail page, and its setup and assignment rules are built around those objects, so an org tracking leads in a custom object has nothing for the agent to engage.
Two notes for the exam. The option's wording is slightly narrow (contact and person account are supported alongside the standard Lead), and the agent has been renamed Agentforce Lead Nurturing, so current articles are filed under that name.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (only works on Opportunities) — this agent nurtures top-of-funnel prospects, answers their questions and books meetings, rather than working open deals.
Option C (only supports custom objects associated with Accounts) — the agent does not work on custom objects at all; it is built around lead, contact and person account.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.sales_agent_sdr_assign_manually.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.sales_agent_sdr_intro.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question:
Universal Containers (UC) wants to implement an AI-powered customer service agent that can:
Retrieve proprietary policy documents that are stored as PDFs.
Ensure responses are grounded in approved company data, not generic LLM knowledge.
What should UC do first?
optionA: Set up an Agentforce Data Library for AI retrieval of policy documents.
optionB: Expand the AI agent's scope to search all Salesforce records.
optionC: Add the files to the content, and then select the data library option.
explanation:
Setting up an Agentforce Data Library for AI retrieval of policy documents is the first step, because UC must first establish a foundation for the AI to access and use this data. A data library lets UC upload the PDF policy documents, index them into Data Cloud's vector database, and make them available for AI retrieval. That is what lets the agent perform retrieval-augmented generation, grounding its responses in the specific, approved content from the PDFs rather than relying on generic LLM knowledge, which meets both requirements.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (expand the agent's scope to search all Salesforce records) — too broad and unnecessary; the requirement is about PDF policy documents, not all Salesforce data, so widening scope is premature and does nothing to index the PDFs.
Option C (add the files to the content, then select the data library option) — vague and not a precise process; adding files to Salesforce Content without a data library indexing them does not enable AI retrieval. Setting up the library is what encompasses the upload and indexing.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_concept.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_data_sources.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Coral Cloud Resorts needs consistent pass/fail logic for agent testing. Which Testing Center capability provides that?
optionA: Use customer rating as a proxy for correctness.
optionB: Run a script on event logs to identify the failed utterances.
optionC: Use structured batch testing with validation per test utterance,
explanation:
Structured batch testing with validation per test utterance is the capability, because consistent pass or fail comes from validating each test case against an expectation. That is what Testing Center's batch testing does: you upload structured scenarios, and each one is evaluated for response accuracy, subagent and action selection, and knowledge retrieval, so the same suite produces the same verdicts run after run.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (customer rating as a proxy for correctness) — measures satisfaction after the fact and mixes in everything else about the interaction; it cannot serve as a gate.
Option B (a script on event logs to identify failed utterances) — tells you what happened but has no expected result to compare against, so what counts as a failure drifts with whoever wrote the script.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Amid their busy schedules, sales reps at Universal Containers dedicate time to follow up with prospects and existing clients via email regarding renewals or new deals. They spend many hours throughout the week reviewing past communications and details about their customers before performing their outreach. Which standard Agent action helps sales reps draft personalized emails to prospects by generating text based on previous successful communications?
optionA: Agent Action: Summarize Record
optionB: Agent Action: Find Similar Opportunities
optionC: Agent Action: Draft or Revise Sales Email
explanation:
Draft or Revise Sales Email is the standard action, so nothing has to be built. Salesforce ships Draft or Revise Email, which creates or revises a draft to a recipient based on the user's request (recipient, subject and body), ready to send from the Salesforce email composer, and it runs on the Einstein Sales Emails permission. Grounded in the record and the account's history, that is what saves the rep the review-everything-first hour.
Naming note: the action is documented today as Draft or Revise Email, without 'Sales' in the title.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Summarize Record) — condenses a record for reading; it does not draft the outreach.
Option B (Find Similar Opportunities) — surfaces comparable deals; it does not write an email.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_ref_draft_or_revise_email.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_ref.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers recently added a custom flow for processing returns and created a new Agent Action. Which action should the company take to ensure the Agentforce Service Agent can run this new flow as part of the new Agent Action?
optionA: Recreate the flow using the Agentforce agent user.
optionB: Assign the Manage Users permission to the Agentforce Agent user.
optionC: Assign the Run Flows permission to the Agentforce Agent user.
explanation:
Assigning the Run Flows permission to the Agentforce Agent user is the standard, documented step to enable flow execution in Agent Actions. The Agentforce Service Agent operates under a dedicated agent user with its own profile or permission set, and to execute a flow as part of an Agent Action that user must have the Run Flows permission, either via its profile or a permission set (or access granted to that individual flow). That ensures the agent can invoke the custom flow for processing returns, in line with Salesforce's security model and Agentforce setup requirements.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (recreate the flow using the Agentforce agent user) — flows are authored by admins or developers, not recreated by the agent user; the issue is the flow's execution permission, not its creation context.
Option B (assign the Manage Users permission) — Manage Users allows user management, such as creating or editing users, which is unrelated to running flows; it is excessive and irrelevant.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_actions_common_perms.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) recently rolled out Einstein Generative AI capabilities and has created a custom prompt to summarize case records. Users have reported that the case summaries generated are not returning the appropriate information. What is a possible explanation for the poor prompt performance?
optionA: The prompt template version is incompatible with the chosen LLM.
optionB: The data being used for grounding is incorrect or incomplete.
optionC: The Einstein Trust Layer is incorrectly configured.
explanation:
Incorrect or incomplete grounding data is the likely explanation, because a summary is only as good as what the prompt was given. Grounding is what puts the record's real content into the prompt through merge fields, and if the fields chosen are the wrong ones, empty on these records, or missing the case comments where the substance lives, the model writes a fluent summary of thin material. That is the first thing to check when output is consistently off-target.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (template version incompatible with the chosen LLM) — a version carries a model configuration, and a mismatch fails loudly at deployment rather than quietly degrading summaries; it does not produce wrong-but-plausible content.
Option C (Einstein Trust Layer incorrectly configured) — the Trust Layer masks sensitive values and applies system policies; a misconfiguration there shows up as masked placeholders or refusals, not as a summary drawing on the wrong information.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce wants to include data from the response of external service invocation (REST API callout) into the prompt template. How should the Agentforce Specialist meet this requirement?
optionA: Convert the JSON to an XML merge field.
optionB: Use External Service Record merge fields.
optionC: Use "Add Prompt Instructions" flow element.
explanation:
Using the "Add Prompt Instructions" flow element is the way, because Salesforce has a purpose-built element for this. The Add Prompt Instructions element provides data in the form of prompt instructions that are merged into a prompt template in Prompt Builder, and it exists only in template-triggered prompt flows. So the pattern is: the flow makes the callout (through an HTTP Callout action or an External Services invocable action) and then merges the returned data into the template with Add Prompt Instructions.
That is the documented route because the template itself cannot call an API. What Prompt Builder can reference through Insert Resource is record fields, flows, Apex, Data 360 DMOs, and related lists; an external service reaches the prompt through the flow or Apex entry in that list.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (convert the JSON to an XML merge field) — not a supported step, and it would not change what the template can reference.
Option B (External Service Record merge fields) — no such merge field type exists; an external service is not a resource the template can merge directly.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_add_prompt.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_concepts_trigger_prompt_template_capability.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: B->C. Salesforce documents no External Service Record merge field for prompt templates — the grounding resources are record fields, flows, Apex, Data 360 DMOs, and related lists. The documented way to merge callout data into a template is the Add Prompt Instructions element in a template-triggered prompt flow, whose stated purpose is providing data that is merged into a prompt template.

question: Universal Containers wants support agents to use Agentforce to ask questions about its product tutorials and product guides. What should the Agentforce Specialist do to meet this requirement?
optionA: Create a prompt template for product tutorials and guides.
optionB: Add an Answer Questions custom field in the product object for tutorial instructions.
optionC: Publish product tutorials and guides as Knowledge articles.
explanation:
Publishing product tutorials and guides as Knowledge articles is what makes the material reachable. The Answer Questions with Knowledge action answers a user's question from relevant knowledge articles and uploaded files, and a data library indexes those articles so retrieval is semantic rather than keyword, so tutorials and guides that live as articles become answerable content, and updates flow through as the index picks them up.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a prompt template for tutorials and guides) — a prompt template shapes how a response is written but has no corpus of its own to draw on.
Option B (an Answer Questions custom field on the product object) — puts prose on a record where nothing indexes or ranks it; the agent cannot retrieve it as knowledge.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_ref_answer_questions_with_knowledge.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_concept.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers implements Custom Agent Actions to enhance its customer service operations. The development team needs to understand the core components of a Custom Agent Action to ensure proper configuration and functionality. What should the development team review in the Custom Agent Action configuration to identify one of the core components of a Custom Agent Action?
optionA: Action Triggers
optionB: Instructions
optionC: Output Types
explanation:
Instructions are the core component to review, because instructions are what make an action usable by an agent. Salesforce describes action instructions as telling the agent what your action does and when to use it, and says to plan and test them carefully when you create a custom action, because the reasoning engine reads the action's name and instructions, including input and output instructions, when deciding what to run.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Action Triggers) — there is no action trigger to configure; an action is selected by the reasoning engine, not fired by an event.
Option C (Output Types) — output types describe the data an action returns and are part of its inputs and outputs, but it is the output instructions, telling the agent how to use what came back, that are the configured component.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_instructions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_custom.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What is the main purpose of Prompt Builder?
optionA: A tool for developers to use in Visual Studio Code that creates prompts for Apex programming, assisting developers in writing code more efficiently.
optionB: A tool that enables companies to create reusable prompts for large language models (LLMs), bringing generative AI responses to their flow of work
optionC: A tool within Salesforce offering real-time Al-powered suggestions and guidance to users, Improving productivity and decision-making.
explanation:
A tool that enables companies to create reusable prompts for large language models, bringing generative AI responses to their flow of work, is Prompt Builder's main purpose. It lets organizations create and configure reusable prompts that interact with Salesforce data through grounding and are surfaced in workflows, producing tailored and consistent AI-generated content in business contexts such as customer service and sales.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a Visual Studio Code tool for Apex prompts) — Prompt Builder is not a developer tool for Apex programming; that description is closer to Einstein for Developers.
Option C (real-time AI-powered suggestions and guidance to users) — Prompt Builder is not limited to real-time suggestions; it is where companies author and manage how AI-driven responses are generated and used in their workflows.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_template_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers' internal auditing team asks an Agentforce to verify that address information is properly masked in the prompt being generated. How should the Agentforce Specialist verify the privacy of the masked data in the Einstein Trust Layer?
optionA: Enable data encryption on the address field
optionB: Review the platform event logs
optionC: Inspect the AI audit trail
explanation:
Inspecting the AI audit trail is how masking is verified, because masking is verified from audit data, not from the org's ordinary logs. Salesforce's guidance after configuring data masking is to verify that sensitive data is masked and monitor it over time using generative AI audit data (the audit trail), which records Trust Layer functionality such as masking and toxicity detection and is stored in Data 360 for reporting.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (enable data encryption on the address field) — a different control entirely; encryption protects data at rest in Salesforce and says nothing about what text was sent to the model.
Option B (review the platform event logs) — platform event logs do not carry the prompt's masked content.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_audit_data_mask.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_audit_trail.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) is looking to improve its sales team's productivity by providing real-time insights and recommendations during customer interactions. Why should UC consider using Agentforce Sales Agent?
optionA: To track customer interactions for future analysis
optionB: To automate the entire sales process for maximum efficiency
optionC: To streamline the sales process and increase conversion rates
explanation:
Streamlining the sales process and increasing conversion rates is why UC should consider Agentforce Sales Agent. Salesforce positions its sales agents as productivity multipliers around the selling process rather than replacements for it: they generate prioritised prospect lists, synthesise an account's calls, meetings and email history, nurture leads autonomously, and coach reps on their pitch, work that moves deals along and gives reps back the hours they spent preparing.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (track customer interactions for future analysis) — describes activity capture, which is a data-collection feature rather than a reason to deploy an agent.
Option B (automate the entire sales process) — no documented sales agent automates the entire sales process; each covers a defined slice with a human still selling.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.sales_cloud_agents.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_explore_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Al Specialist is tasked with creating a prompt template for a sales team. The template needs to generate a summary of all related opportunities for a given Account. Which grounding technique should the Al Specialist use to include data from the related list of opportunities in the prompt template?
optionA: Use the merge fields to reference a custom related list of opportunities.
optionB: Use merge fields to reference the default related list of opportunities.
optionC: Use formula fields to reference the Einstein related list of opportunities.
explanation:
Using merge fields to reference the default related list of opportunities is the grounding technique, because related list grounding is built in and nothing custom is required. Prompt Builder supports related list merge fields, and the fields available come from the page layout of the parent object for the current user, so the Account's standard Opportunities related list can be merged into the template directly.
Two rules that come with it are worth knowing. Only related lists present on the object's page layout are available for grounding, and record-level filters are not applied to what is retrieved; the data is rendered as JSON in the resolution. Also note the documented exception: Activities related lists on objects such as Account and Case are not supported.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (merge fields for a custom related list of opportunities) — no custom related list is needed; the standard Opportunities related list on the Account layout is already available for grounding.
Option C (formula fields referencing the Einstein related list) — formula fields are not a grounding mechanism, and there is no Einstein related list to reference.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_related_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Choose 1 option. Cloud Kicks (CK) recently finished the development of a new prompt template that uses its own large language model (LLM). CK is deploying a prompt template from a sandbox to a production org, and is receiving an error. When trying to deploy the change set, CK is getting an error related to the LLM used in the prompt template. What is the cause of the error?
optionA: The prompt does not specify that it is a custom LLM.
optionB: BYOLLM is not yet supported for in prompt templates in production.
optionC: The name of the LLM does not match in sandbox and production.
explanation:
The name of the LLM not matching between sandbox and production is the cause. Salesforce states this exact failure in its change set considerations for prompt templates: when you deploy a template with a custom large language model configuration, verify that the target org has a model with the same name; if the model name doesn't match, the deployment fails. A BYO-LLM configuration is not carried across by the change set, so production has to already hold a model registered under the same name.
Related considerations from the same page: a version does not auto-activate during deployment unless Deploy Prompt Templates is enabled in the target org, and an active version of a template in use cannot be deleted.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the prompt does not specify that it is a custom LLM) — a template does not declare that its model is custom; the model configuration it points to is either resolvable in the target org or it is not.
Option B (BYOLLM not yet supported in production) — BYO-LLM is supported in production; nothing about the feature is sandbox-only.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_considerations_changeset.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_changing_llm_configurations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What is automatically created when a custom search index is created in Data Cloud?
optionA: A retriever that shares the name of the custom search index.
optionB: A dynamic retriever to allow runtime selection of retriever parameters without manual configuration.
optionC: A predefined Apex retriever class that can be edited by a developer to meet specific needs.
explanation:
A retriever that shares the name of the custom search index is the answer the exam wants, and it describes behaviour Salesforce has since retired; both halves are worth knowing. Historically, creating a search index in Data Cloud automatically produced a default retriever named after the index, which you could then use in Prompt Builder or Flow. Salesforce's current documentation states plainly that Data 360 no longer creates a default retriever automatically when you create a search index, though existing default retrievers still work. So today you create the retriever yourself: an individual retriever in AI Models, where you select its search index, define filters, and specify what it returns.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (a dynamic retriever with runtime parameter selection) — there is no dynamic retriever that selects its parameters at runtime without configuration.
Option C (a predefined Apex retriever class) — no Apex retriever class is generated for a developer to edit.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_create.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question:
Universal Containers has set up a Service Agent to allow customers to look up their order status. The topic setup includes:
Name: Order Inquiry Classification.
Description: Handles user requests to look up order status, including tracking details and delivery estimates for orders placed within the last 90 days.
Scope: Your job is only to assist authenticated users in looking up the status of their orders placed within the last 90 days. If the order is pending delivery, provide the tracking number and estimated delivery date. Do not handle inquiries for orders older than 90 days.
Which information will be used by the Agentforce reasoning engine to choose this topic?
optionA: Topic Name and Classification Description
optionB: Topic Name and Scope
optionC: Classification Description and Scope
explanation:
Topic Name and Classification Description are what the reasoning engine uses to choose the topic. Topic selection and topic behaviour read different fields, and this question asks about selection. Salesforce describes the classification step precisely: the reasoning engine compares the recent conversation history, including the user's most recent message, to the names and classification descriptions of all the subagents available to the agent.
Scope matters afterwards. Once a subagent is selected, the engine collects the subagent's name, scope, and instructions, plus the names and instructions of its actions, to decide what to do next, which is where 'only assist authenticated users' and the 90-day boundary do their work, constraining behaviour rather than winning the match. That distinction is worth carrying into the exam: a vague classification description means the topic is never selected, while a vague scope means it is selected and then behaves badly.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Topic Name and Scope) — scope is read after selection to govern behaviour; it is not compared against the utterance to choose the topic.
Option C (Classification Description and Scope) — omits the name, which is compared alongside the classification description, and includes scope, which is not used for selection.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_reasoning_engine.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: C->A. Salesforce documents the classification step as comparing the conversation history to the names and classification descriptions of the available subagents. Scope is collected only after a subagent has been selected, to guide its behaviour, so it is not part of choosing the topic.

question: Choose 1 option. What does it mean when a prompt template version is described as immutable?
optionA: After a prompt template version is activated, no further changes can be saved to that version.
optionB: Only the latest version of a template can be activated.
optionC: Every modification on a template will be saved as a new version automatically.
explanation:
That after a prompt template version is activated no further changes can be saved to that version is what immutable means. Salesforce puts it in one line: activating a template version makes it immutable, and even if deactivated, any version that was ever active remains immutable. To change such a template you save it as a new version, which is also why each version can carry its own model configuration, with only the activated version's configuration in use.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (only the latest version can be activated) — any version can be activated, not only the latest, which is what makes versioning useful for comparing constructions.
