Option C (Sales Summary) — summarizes sales records such as accounts and opportunities, not the content of a call.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.eci_call_summaries.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question:
A service manager wants to use Salesforce Prompt Builder to help agents summarize customer case notes after a support call. The summary should:
Capture the customer's issue, troubleshooting steps taken, and next actions.
Be no longer than five sentences.
Use plain language with no technical jargon.
If no next action is identified, explicitly state "No next action required."
Which key prompt constructs meet this requirement?
optionA: Role, Task, LLM Clarity Score, and Format
optionB: Role, Task, Token Size Limit, and Format
optionC: Task, Context, Constraints, and Format
explanation:
Task, Context, Constraints, and Format are the constructs the requirement maps onto: the task is summarizing case notes, the context is the issue, steps and next actions, the constraints are five sentences, plain language and the fixed fallback phrase, and the format is how the summary is laid out. Salesforce's Ingredients of a Prompt Template names the same building blocks under its own labels — a goal, the setting and data, instructions and guidelines the model must follow, and style and tone.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (includes an "LLM Clarity Score") — not a prompt construct; no such score exists in Prompt Builder.
Option B (includes a "Token Size Limit") — a model limit, not something you write into a prompt, and it does not express the five-sentence rule.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_template_ingredients.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is evaluating Einstein Generative AI features to improve the productivity of the service center operation. Which features should the Agentforce Specialist recommend?
optionA: Service Replies and Case Summaries
optionB: Service Replies and Work Summaries
optionC: Reply Recommendations and Sales Summaries
explanation:
Service Replies and Case Summaries is the exam's answer: Service Replies drafts responses for reps, and case summaries give reps a fast overview of a case. Be aware that the feature names have moved. Salesforce now documents case summaries as part of Einstein Work Summaries — "AI-generated conversation and case summaries", with a Case channel in beta — and the stand-alone Case Summaries feature was a Winter '25 pilot. On current documentation, option B (Service Replies and Work Summaries) describes the same capability under today's name, so this item has two defensible answers.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Service Replies and Work Summaries) — not wrong on today's documentation; the exam keys A, which names the case-summary capability explicitly.
Option C (Reply Recommendations and Sales Summaries) — Reply Recommendations is the older predictive feature and Sales Summaries is a Sales Cloud feature, not service-center productivity.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.cc_generative_ai_work_summaries.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: Two options name real features. Service Replies with Case Summaries is the exam answer, but Salesforce now delivers case summaries through Einstein Work Summaries ("AI-generated conversation and case summaries", with a Case channel in beta); the separate Case Summaries feature was a Winter '25 pilot. So option B (Service Replies and Work Summaries) is at least as defensible on current documentation.

question: An Agentforce Agent has been developed with multiple topics and Agent Actions that use flows and Apex. Which options are available for deploying these to production?
optionA: Deploy the flows and Apex using normal deployment tools and manually create the agent-related items in production.
optionB: Use only change sets because the Salesforce CLI does not currently support the deployment of agent-related metadata.
optionC: Deploy flows, Apex, and all agent-related items using either change sets or the Salesforce CLI /Metadata API.
explanation:
Deploying the flows, Apex and all agent-related items using either change sets or the Salesforce CLI / Metadata API is correct. Salesforce's knowledge article Agentforce Deployment with Change Set lists the agent components that go into an outbound change set — GenAiFunction and GenAiPlugin definitions, the Bot, flows and Apex classes — and stresses including every interdependent component; the Agentforce DX guide documents retrieving and deploying the same agent metadata with the CLI.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (deploy code, then recreate agent items by hand) — the agent itself is metadata and deploys with the rest.
Option B (change sets only; the CLI can't deploy agents) — the CLI and Metadata API deploy agent metadata; that is what Agentforce DX is for.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005232697&language=en_US&type=1
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/agent-dx-deploy-metadata.html

question: Universal Containers wants to incorporate CRM data as well-formatted JSON in a prompt to a large language model (LLM). What is an important consideration for this requirement?
optionA: "CRM data to JSON" checkbox must be selected when creating a prompt template.
optionB: Apex code can be used to return a JSON formatted merge field.
optionC: JSON format should be enabled in Prompt Builder Settings.
explanation:
Apex code returning a JSON-formatted merge field is the consideration. Salesforce's Grounding with Apex Merge Fields says an Apex merge field can return data from a SOQL query or an external API, and that "Apex is also effective if you want to generate well-formatted JSON or do programmatic data filtering" — typically an invocable method whose response serializes the records with JSON.serialize().
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a "CRM data to JSON" checkbox) — no such checkbox exists on a prompt template.
Option C (a JSON format setting in Prompt Builder Settings) — no such setting; formatting is done in the grounding code.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_apex.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers needs to bring individual customer warranties from an external system into Data Cloud. They want Agentforce to return warranty-related responses only for accounts whose warranty status is active. Which search approach should the Agentforce Specialist configure to ensure warranty-related information is retrieved correctly?
optionA: Depend on Agentforce instructions to enforce warranty constraints and include only WarrantyStatus = Active results.
optionB: Store the account's warranty status in an Agentforce custom variable to dynamically filter warranties during retrieval.
optionC: Use Hybrid Search and apply pre-filtering in a new custom retriever for matching accounts and where the WarrantyStatus = Active field.
explanation:
Using Hybrid Search with pre-filtering in a new custom retriever, matching accounts where WarrantyStatus = Active, is the approach. A custom (individual) retriever lets you "define filters to narrow the search results" on fields the search index exposes for filtering, and the search index supports pre-filter fields, so inactive warranties never reach the prompt. Hybrid search adds keyword matching on exact values alongside semantic recall.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (rely on agent instructions to drop inactive results) — instructions are not a filter; the LLM can still see and use the wrong records.
Option B (a custom variable to filter retrieval) — agent variables do not filter what a retriever returns; the filter belongs on the retriever.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_create.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_search_index_reference.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_hybridsearch_fusion_ranking.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers would like to route SMS text messages to a service rep from an Agentforce Service Agent. Which Service Channel should the company use in the flow to ensure it's routed properly?
optionA: Messaging
optionB: Route Work Action
optionC: Live Agent
explanation:
Messaging is the service channel for SMS. SMS runs on Salesforce's Messaging channels, and a service agent on a messaging channel transfers conversations to a rep or queue through an outbound Omni-Channel flow that routes the Messaging work item.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Route Work Action) — the flow element that does the routing, not a service channel.
Option C (Live Agent) — the legacy chat channel, not the one SMS messaging sessions use.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.service_agent_escalation.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is auditing its AI architecture and needs to ensure that its developers are restricted to using only specifically approved large language models. How should an Agentforce Specialist manage and prevent unapproved models from being accessed across the organization?
optionA: Apply an Attribute-Based Access Control policy within the Einstein Trust Layer to block prompts from routing to unapproved large language models
optionB: Write a strict system instruction within Agent Builder stating, "Never use external models for reasoning"
optionC: Ensure only approved large language models are enabled in the Model Provider section under Einstein Setup
explanation:
Ensuring only approved LLMs are enabled in the model provider settings in Einstein Setup is the control. Salesforce's Large Language Model Support page says "a Salesforce admin can disable a model provider" and links Manage Model Provider Access, which lets you "Choose which Large Language Model (LLM) providers to allow or not allow in your organization" — an org-wide platform control rather than a prompt-level request.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (an attribute-based access policy in the Trust Layer) — the Trust Layer masks, audits and scores content; it does not govern which providers are enabled.
Option B (a system instruction telling the agent not to use external models) — an instruction to the LLM cannot restrict which model the platform routes to.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_large_language_model_support.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) stores case details and updates in several custom fields and custom objects related to the case. UC would like its Agentforce Service Agent to be able to provide information in these fields and related records as part of an answer back to its customers when the customer is asking for updates. Which best practice should UC follow to grant access to this information for the Agentforce Service Agent?
optionA: Update the Object and Field access in the AgentforceServiceAgentUserPsg permission set group that is already assigned to the Agentforce Service Agent user.
optionB: Create a new permission set with the Einstein Agent License and enable Read access to the custom fields and custom objects, and assign it to the Agentforce Service Agent user.
optionC: Update the Object and Field access in the Einstein Agent User Profile so that the Agentforce Service Agents will always get the necessary access.
explanation:
Creating a new permission set with the Einstein Agent license, granting Read on the custom objects and fields, and assigning it to the Agentforce Service Agent user is the best practice. Salesforce's Configure Service Agent Access says the agent user is created with minimal access and you expand it on the principle of least privilege, either by editing the agent's own [Agent_Name]_Permissions permission set or — "If you want to create a different permission set for your agent user" — by making sure it is "associated with the Einstein Agent license and Einstein Agent User profile".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (edit object and field access on AgentforceServiceAgentUserPsg) — a permission set group bundles permission sets; object and field access is granted in a permission set, not on the group.
Option C (edit the Einstein Agent User profile) — widens every agent that shares the profile; permission sets are the documented, least-privilege route.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_user.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed updating object and field access on the AgentforceServiceAgentUserPsg permission set group. A permission set group holds no object or field permissions of its own, and Configure Service Agent Access says to edit the agent's [Agent_Name]_Permissions permission set or, "If you want to create a different permission set for your agent user, make sure that it's associated with the Einstein Agent license and Einstein Agent User profile" — which is option B.

question: Pinnacle Healthcare is enhancing its agent and Agent Script implementation to improve patient scheduling and care coordination. The head of compliance has identified a need to ensure deterministic behavior for agents when verifying patient information before scheduling appointments. The process must enforce compliance by gating downstream actions, for example, scheduling, until patient verification is complete. What is the most appropriate approach the Agentforce Specialist should recommend while adhering to standard configuration guidelines?
optionA: Call a custom Apex @InvocableMethod to enforce the verification logic and dynamically update the scheduling action availability.
optionB: Use @utils.setVariables to update a mutable session variable for patient verification status and gate scheduling actions with available when.
optionC: Use template expressions in the action descriptions to dynamically display instructions based on the verification status.
explanation:
Using @utils.setVariables to update a mutable session variable for verification status, and gating the scheduling actions with available when, is the approach. The Agent Script tools reference says you "can use the available when parameter to deterministically specify when the tool is available", and Salesforce's filtering pattern notes that when the condition is not met "the LLM can't access the subagent or reasoning action" — so scheduling is simply not callable until verification sets the flag.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (an invocable Apex method that toggles action availability) — actions do not change their own availability; availability is declared on the tool.
Option C (template expressions in action descriptions) — changes the wording the LLM reads, which still leaves the choice to the LLM.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-utils.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-tools.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-patterns-filtering.html

question: Universal Containers has successfully chunked and vectorized its unstructured meeting notes into a Data 360 search index. An Agentforce Specialist needs to connect this data to a prompt template to dynamically refine search criteria and retrieve the most relevant information. How should the specialist achieve this?
optionA: Create a Flex template referencing a data lake object (DLO).
optionB: Create a Flex template referencing a retriever in the prompt template.
optionC: Create a Flex template referencing the data model object (DMO).
explanation:
Creating a Flex template that references a retriever is how the indexed meeting notes reach the prompt. Salesforce's Retrieve Data page says retrievers "search and return relevant data from a search Index" and that "In Prompt Builder, you ground a prompt template with knowledge by inserting and configuring a retriever", which at run time supplies the most relevant chunks for the query.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (reference the data lake object) — the DLO is raw ingested data, not the chunked, vectorized index.
Option C (reference the data model object) — the DMO holds structured records; semantic search over chunks goes through a retriever.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) is preparing and defining success criteria for Agentforce Testing Center test cases. Which details should UC specify as the expected output to ensure the tests accurately reflect the agent's functionality?
optionA: Expected Topic API Name
optionB: Expected Flow API Name
optionC: Expected Prompt Template Name
explanation:
The expected topic API name (topics are now called subagents) is the expected output to specify. Testing Center's default evaluations include a subagent assertion, which "determines if your agent selected the correct subagents based on the utterance", alongside an action assertion and a response evaluation, so each test case names the subagent it should route to.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (expected flow API name) — tests assert on actions, not on the flow behind an action.
Option C (expected prompt template name) — not an expectation field in a Testing Center test case.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center_evaluations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to create a prompt template that consistently extracts a customer's specific product model number and quantity from an email inquiry to draft a response back to the customer. Which best practice should UC implement to achieve this goal?
optionA: Incorporate open-ended questions to encourage detailed responses
optionB: Provide clear, positive instructions and use few-shot examples
optionC: Use a high temperature setting to increase creative output
explanation:
Providing clear, positive instructions and using few-shot examples is the best practice for consistent extraction. Salesforce's prompt-engineering Trailhead unit defines few-shot prompting as giving "the AI a few examples of the task you want it to complete" so it "learns the pattern", and Prompt Builder's best practices call for direct instructions about exactly what to generate.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (open-ended questions) — invites variation, the opposite of consistent extraction.
Option C (a high temperature) — raises randomness; extraction wants a low, deterministic setting.
References:
https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/prompt-engineering-techniques/improve-prompts-using-different-prompt-techniques
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers tests out a new Einstein Generative AI feature for its sales team to create personalized and contextualized emails for its customers. Sometimes, users find that the draft email contains placeholders for attributes that could have been derived from the recipient's contact record. What is the most likely explanation for why the draft email shows these placeholders?
optionA: The user does not have permission to access the fields.
optionB: The user's locale language is not supported by Prompt Builder.
optionC: The user does not have Einstein Sales Emails permission assigned.
explanation:
The user not having permission to access the fields is the most likely cause. Salesforce's Considerations for Einstein Generative AI Sales Emails says "Field-level security is enforced. If users don't have access to a field used for email grounding, then that field data isn't used. The sales rep sees a placeholder to customize as needed" — and a blank field produces the same kind of placeholder.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (the user's locale isn't supported) — an unsupported language would affect the whole draft, not individual attributes.
Option C (missing Einstein Sales Emails permission) — without it the user could not draft the email at all.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.einstein_sales_emails_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The compliance team at Universal Containers has determined that a specific customer service prompt must only process data through a secure, self-hosted Amazon Bedrock model and must be prevented from accessing the default OpenAI models. How should the Agentforce Specialist configure this specific model routing?
optionA: Assign a permission set to the dedicated Agent User that restricts Read access to the default Salesforce large language model (LLM) metadata records.
optionB: Configure a Data 360 Private Connect endpoint that automatically reroutes all Agentforce requests away from the default large language model (LLM) Gateway.
optionC: Register the model as a BYOLLM in Einstein Studio, then explicitly select this model when configuring the prompt template.
explanation:
Registering the Bedrock model as a BYOLLM in Einstein Studio, then explicitly selecting it when configuring the prompt template, is the routing. Bring Your Own LLM connects a provider's model "using your own account" as a foundation model in AI Models, and Prompt Builder lets each template choose its model configuration, so this one prompt runs on the approved model while others keep their defaults.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a permission set restricting read on default LLM metadata) — model selection is not controlled by record access on metadata.
Option B (a Private Connect endpoint that reroutes all requests) — Private Connect secures network paths; it does not choose a model, and "all requests" is broader than one prompt.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/einstein/genai/guide/get-started-einstein-studio.html
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_changing_llm_configurations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: During configuration, Universal Containers (UC) forgot to grant Knowledge access to the Agentforce Service Agent. Which permission must UC add for the agent to interact with Knowledge articles and answer customer questions effectively?
optionA: Allow View Knowledge and Run Flows
optionB: Access Knowledge records and fields, and Allow View Knowledge
optionC: Access Custom Objects and Manage External Users
explanation:
Access to Knowledge records and fields together with Allow View Knowledge is the permission. Salesforce's retriever setup page says that for the Knowledge object the user needs "read access to the Knowledge object and has the App Permission: Allow View Knowledge" — both halves, because one grants the records and the other the Knowledge app.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Allow View Knowledge and Run Flows) — misses the object and field access to the Knowledge records themselves.
Option C (Access Custom Objects and Manage External Users) — unrelated to reading Knowledge articles.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_create.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Which scenario best illustrates the use of Model Context Protocol (MCP) in an enterprise AI deployment?
optionA: A legal assistant agent using MCP to dynamically find a document classification API to analyze case files
optionB: A customer service agent engaging another agent in real-time conversation to resolve tickets
optionC: A sales agent discovering other agents' capabilities using Agent Cards
explanation:
A legal assistant agent using MCP to dynamically find a document classification API is the MCP scenario. Salesforce describes MCP as "An open, vendor-neutral standard ... that defines how AI agents connect to external tools, data sources, and APIs": an MCP server exposes tools and the agent picks the right one through natural language.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (one agent conversing with another to resolve tickets) — agent-to-agent collaboration is A2A, not MCP.
Option C (discovering other agents through Agent Cards) — Agent Cards are part of A2A.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005317683&language=en_US&type=1
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/mcp.html

question: In a Knowledge-based data library, which capability does enabling the "Filter by Knowledge Data Categories" option provide?
optionA: It applies custom metadata from the selected data categories to the Knowledge articles, aiming to enhance search relevance.
optionB: It organizes the indexed Knowledge articles into separate sections based on their assigned data categories.
optionC: It limits the indexed articles to only those belonging to selected data categories, thereby improving indexing precision.
explanation:
Limiting the indexed articles to those in the selected data categories is what the option does. Salesforce's Use Salesforce Knowledge page says "To filter indexed articles by data category, enable Filter by Knowledge Data Categories. Then, select the categories to include in your data library", which "makes the indexing and grounding more accurate and efficient".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (applies category metadata to articles) — the filter selects articles; it does not tag them.
Option B (organizes articles into sections by category) — it narrows what is indexed; it does not restructure the index.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_select_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Specialist configured Data Masking within the Einstein Trust Layer. How should the Agentforce Specialist begin validating that the correct fields are being masked?
optionA: Use a Flow-based resource in Prompt Builder to debug the fields' merge values using Flow Debugger.
optionB: Request the Einstein Generative AI Audit Data from the Security section of the Setup menu.
optionC: Enable the collection and storage of Einstein Generative AI Audit Data on the Einstein Feedback setup page.
explanation:
Enabling the collection and storage of Einstein Generative AI audit data is where validation begins. Salesforce's Audit Trail page says that when data masking is on, the audit data "includes the masked prompt text that was sent to an external LLM", and that to access it "you'll need to turn on the Einstein generative AI data collection and storage and install the report package" — without that switch there is nothing to inspect.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (debug merge values with Flow Debugger) — shows the data before the Trust Layer masks it, which is not what you are validating.
Option B (request audit data from the Security section of Setup) — not how audit data is obtained; it has to be collected into Data 360 first.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_audit_trail.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Specialist is building a Flex prompt template. Which best practice should the Agentforce Specialist follow when creating the Flex prompt template?
optionA: Provide the large language model (LLM) with contextual information and give it a role such as a sales or support rep.
optionB: Ground the large language model (LLM) with account data and create a custom field account summary to store the LLM-generated response.
optionC: Ground the large language model (LLM) with a retriever and create a custom field to store the LLM- generated Response.
explanation:
Giving the LLM contextual information and a role, such as a sales or support rep, is the best practice. Salesforce's Best Practices for Building Prompt Templates says "To give the LLM more contextual information, ask it to role play as a character, such as a sales or support representative. Then define the character's goal."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (store the output in a custom account-summary field) — a Field Generation pattern, not a Flex template practice, and unrelated to prompt quality.
Option C (ground with a retriever and store the response in a field) — grounding choice depends on the data; saving to a field is not a prompt-building practice.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has grounded a prompt template with a related list. During user acceptance testing (UAT), users are not getting the correct responses. What is causing this issue?
optionA: The related list is Read Only.
optionB: The related list prompt template option is not enabled.
optionC: The related list is not on the parent object's page layout.
explanation:
The related list not being on the parent object's page layout is the cause. Grounding with Related List Merge Fields says the related list's fields "are based on the page layout of the parent object for the current user", and "If ... a user doesn't have the related list on their parent object's page layout or Read permission on the associated object, no related list data is sent to the LLM."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the related list is read-only) — read-only data is still readable for grounding.
Option B (a related-list option not enabled on the template) — no such template setting exists.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_related_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has a mature Salesforce org with a lot of data in cases and Knowledge articles. UC is concerned that there are many legacy fields, with data that might not be applicable for Einstein AI to draft accurate email responses. Which solution should UC use to ensure Einstein AI can draft responses from a defined data source?
optionA: Service AI Grounding
optionB: Work Summaries
optionC: Service Replies
explanation:
Service AI Grounding is the solution, because it lets UC choose which sources — Knowledge and specific objects and fields — Einstein uses when drafting replies, instead of the whole legacy data set. Grounding decides where reply content comes from; the drafting features then use that curated source.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Work Summaries) — summarizes conversations and cases; it does not control the data behind drafted replies.
Option C (Service Replies) — drafts the replies, but without grounding configuration it does not restrict which fields it draws on.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.cc_generative_ai_work_summaries.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to test agents while preserving real data and isolating from production. Which environment should the company use with Testing Center?
optionA: Use personal developer orgs unrepresentative of production data.
optionB: Use production org directly with test assertions.
optionC: Use sandbox environments replicated from production for safe testing.
explanation:
Sandboxes replicated from production are the environment to test in. Testing Center runs the agent for real — test execution includes agent actions — so testing against production risks changing live records, while a sandbox copy keeps realistic data and isolation; Salesforce also supports Agentforce Data Library in every sandbox type.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (personal developer orgs) — isolated, but their data is not representative of production.
Option B (production with test assertions) — assertions check results; they do not stop actions from modifying live data.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_setup.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What is a valid use case for Data Cloud retrievers?
optionA: Returning relevant data from the vector database to augment a prompt.
optionB: Grounding data from external websites to augment a prompt with RAG.
optionC: Modifying and updating data within the source systems connected to Data Cloud.
explanation:
Returning relevant data from the vector database to augment a prompt is the use case. Salesforce's Retrieve Data page says a retriever searches "and return[s] relevant data from a search Index" and that "Retrievers augment prompt templates by providing relevant, specialized grounding information for prompts."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (grounding from external websites) — Data Cloud retrievers search Data 360 search indexes; web content uses a separate web retriever or the Search the Web action.
Option C (modifying data in source systems) — retrievers are read-only search; they never write back.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A company needs to ensure customers always receive answers based on the most current version of support documentation. What should an Agentforce Specialist recommend?
optionA: Use a file-based Agentforce Data Library (ADL) and enable the version management setting to ensure the agent always retrieves the latest document.
optionB: Use a knowledge-based Agentforce Data Library (ADL); knowledge articles have native versioning built in, so agents automatically retrieve the current published version.
optionC: Use either Agentforce Data Library (ADL) type; both automatically serve the most recent content once the search index rebuilds.
explanation:
A knowledge-based Agentforce Data Library is the recommendation, because Knowledge manages versions and only the current published version is indexed. Salesforce's Use Salesforce Knowledge page says "Only published articles are considered for the data library", so a new published version replaces the old one in what the agent retrieves.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a file-based library with version management) — file libraries have no version-management setting; an updated file is simply another file.
Option C (either type works once the index rebuilds) — file libraries keep serving old uploads until they are removed.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_select_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Cloud Kicks has long, complex legal agreements. An Agentforce agent must be able to retrieve specific clauses that are often nested within larger sections. The standard chunking method is failing to capture the full context of these clauses. Which chunking strategy should an administrator use to preserve the structure of the documents?
optionA: Implement a smaller chunk size.
optionB: Implement a larger chunk size.
optionC: Implement a keyword-based chunking strategy.
explanation:
A larger chunk size preserves nested clauses. The chunk size is set by the Max Token setting (512 by default), and Salesforce's Chunking Strategies page notes that raising it lets Data 360 "Combine adjacent small sections into a larger chunk, optimizing for chunk size without sacrificing coherence", so a clause stays together with its surrounding definitions.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a smaller chunk size) — splits clauses away from their context, which is the failure described.
Option C (keyword-based chunking) — not a Data 360 strategy; the documented ones are section-aware, semantic passage extraction, conversation-based, prepend-field and code.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_search_index_supported_chunking_strategies.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_search_index_max_token_setting.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Specialist at Universal Containers is working on a prompt template to generate personalized emails for product demonstration requests from customers. It is important for the AI-generated email to adhere strictly to the guidelines, using only associated opportunity information, and to encourage the recipient to take the desired action. How should the Agentforce Specialist include these instructions on a new line in the prompt template?
optionA: Surround them with triple quotes (""").
optionB: Make sure merged fields are defined.
optionC: Use curly brackets {} to encapsulate instructions.
explanation:
Surrounding the instructions with triple quotes (""") is the method. Salesforce's Best Practices for Building Prompt Templates says "To help the LLM differentiate between context and instructions, create an instructions section in your prompt template. On a separate line, enter Instructions:, then surround your instructions with triple quotes."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (make sure merged fields are defined) — merge fields supply data; they do not mark instructions.
Option C (curly brackets) — braces denote merge-field syntax, not an instruction block.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_template_ingredients.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The VP of Service at Universal Containers requires a report showing weekly deflection rate trends and escalation volumes for the Agentforce Service Agent over the past 90 days. Which approach should the Agentforce Specialist recommend?
optionA: Enable Agentforce Health Monitoring to configure escalation rate alert thresholds and export the resulting trend data into a Tableau dashboard aligned with the VP of Service's reporting requirements
optionB: Use Agent Analytics within Agentforce Observability, which provides Tableau-powered dashboards with prebuilt deflection rate, escalation volume, and abandonment metrics calculated from agent session data stored in Data 360
optionC: Query the OTEL-compliant Session Tracing Data Model in Data 360 using CRM Analytics to build a custom dashboard with deflection rate calculations and week-over-week escalation comparisons tailored to UC's reporting standards
explanation:
Agent Analytics in Agentforce Observability is the approach. Salesforce describes it as the out-of-the-box way to "Understand usage, effectiveness, and feedback insights of all Agentforce agents", built on session data in Data 360 with prebuilt dashboards, so deflection and escalation trends over 90 days need no custom build.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Health Monitoring alerts exported to Tableau) — health monitoring watches live agent health; it is not the reporting tool for historical trends.
Option C (a custom CRM Analytics dashboard on session tracing) — possible, but a custom build when prebuilt analytics already provide the metrics.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005226932&language=en_US&type=1
https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/observability/

question: During retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) quality testing, an Agentforce Specialist notices that tabular information from a custom Data 360 Document Ingestion Pipeline is losing its context because the data is scattered across multiple separate chunks. What is the most appropriate approach to resolve this?
optionA: Change the search index's parser from the default to Docling.
optionB: Use an ensemble retriever to stitch multiple chunks back together dynamically.
optionC: Switch the search index configuration to use only keyword search scoring.
explanation:
Changing the search index's parser from the default to Docling is the fix. Salesforce's Trailhead on Data 360 content parsing says the Docling Parser "Extracts text and tables with layout understanding" and "delivers superior structural fidelity by interpreting complex elements like multilevel headers, merged cells, and nested tables", while the Default Parser is optimized for linear text.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (an ensemble retriever to stitch chunks together) — works after the damage is done; the table was broken up at parsing time.
Option C (keyword-only search scoring) — changes how chunks are ranked, not how tables are parsed.
References:
https://trailhead.salesforce.com/content/learn/modules/data-cloud-process-content/use-rag-to-bring-unstructured-data-to-agentforce

question: An Agentforce Specialist at Universal Containers observes that the agent frequently directs customers with clear billing inquiries to the general troubleshooting subagent. This misrouting is causing a spike in average handle time and missed service-level agreement targets. The contact center manager requires a solution that is quick to implement but preserves the agent's ability to handle complex, non-linear conversations. What is the most appropriate approach to resolve this?
optionA: Update the agent's global System Instructions to include a list of forbidden keywords for each subagent.
optionB: Audit subagent instructions for semantic competition and implement deterministic filters to guide the planner's selection.
optionC: Create a Router sub-flow that uses a Decision element to manually assign every incoming request to a specific subagent.
explanation:
Auditing subagent instructions for semantic competition and adding deterministic filters to guide the planner is the approach. Salesforce's context-engineering guide says "Clear and distinct subagents prevent overlap and ensure the Reasoning Engine correctly classifies customer requests", and filters with available when hide subagents whose conditions are not met — quick to add, and the agent keeps its conversational flexibility.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (forbidden keywords in global instructions) — keyword rules in prose are brittle and still left to the LLM.
Option C (a Decision-element router flow for every request) — removes the flexible reasoning the manager wants to keep.
References:
https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/guide/
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-patterns-filtering.html

question: What is a key benefit of the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol?
optionA: Provides a standardized framework for cross-vendor agent discovery and communication
optionB: Allows auto-onboard third-party agents without additional contracts, trust scores, or shared identity controls
optionC: Provides a standardized runtime engine for internal agent discovery and communication
explanation:
A standardized framework for cross-vendor agent discovery and communication is A2A's benefit. Salesforce describes A2A as "an open protocol for agent-to-agent communication, enabling agents from different vendors or platforms to discover, invoke, and collaborate with each other", using Agent Cards to publish capabilities.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (auto-onboard third-party agents without contracts or identity controls) — A2A runs over OAuth, and Salesforce governs it through Agent Gateway.
Option C (a runtime engine for internal agent discovery) — A2A is a protocol between vendors; agents inside one org use Salesforce's own orchestration.
References:
https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/ai-agents/agent2agent-protocol/
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005317683&language=en_US&type=1

question: Which statement explains why a company might prefer a hybrid search index in Data Cloud for Agentforce?
optionA: Hybrid search indexes process queries faster than vector search because they eliminate the need for semantic embedding.
optionB: Vector embedding in hybrid search are prefiltered by keyword matches, reducing computational overhead and improving response accuracy.
optionC: Hybrid search indexes support both literal keyword matches and semantic recall, useful when queries mix specific terms and intent.
explanation:
Hybrid search indexes supporting both literal keyword matches and semantic recall is the reason. Salesforce's Hybrid Search Fusion Ranking page says hybrid search "retrieves results from two indexes—keyword and vector" and fuses them, which helps queries that mix exact terms such as product codes with intent.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (faster because no embeddings) — hybrid search still uses the vector index and its embeddings.
Option B (vectors pre-filtered by keyword matches) — the two searches run separately and are fused and reranked, not filtered one by the other.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_hybridsearch_fusion_ranking.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has deployed Agentforce to handle customer order tracking, returns, and loyalty support. The agent needs to balance conversational flexibility for customer inquiries with guaranteed execution of identity verification steps before accessing the account information. The development team is evaluating how to structure the agent's instruction pattern to meet both requirements. Which statement correctly describes hybrid reasoning in Agentforce Agent Script?
optionA: Hybrid reasoning uses multiple large language model (LLM) models simultaneously, with one model handling conversational responses and another model executing deterministic business logic through Flow integration.
optionB: Hybrid reasoning requires Canvas View for declarative instructions and Script View for procedural instructions, as each editor provides different capabilities for the respective instruction types.
optionC: Hybrid reasoning combines declarative natural language instructions that allow large language model (LLM) interpretation with procedural instructions using the -> prefix that enforce guaranteed execution order.
explanation:
Hybrid reasoning combining declarative natural-language instructions with procedural instructions under the -> prefix that enforce execution order is the correct description. Salesforce's Agent Script language page says "Logic instructions (->) run deterministically every time", while the prompt text after | is left to the LLM's interpretation — flexibility and guaranteed steps in the same subagent.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (two LLMs, one conversational and one executing logic through Flow) — one reasoning engine is used; the deterministic part is script logic, not a second model.
Option B (Canvas view for declarative, Script view for procedural) — both views edit the same Agent Script.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-lang.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-flow.html

question: Universal Containers has developed an agent for loan origination workflows that must handle both non-determinism and strict regulatory compliance requirements. The agent needs to ensure that identity verification and credit check steps execute in a precise sequence without deviation. Which statement correctly differentiates these two instruction patterns in Agent Script's hybrid reasoning approach?
optionA: Declarative instructions require Flow execution for business logic, while procedural instructions are native to Agent Script but cannot access external systems or APIs.
optionB: Declarative instructions provide conversational flexibility through large language model interpretation, while procedural instructions use the -> prefix to enforce guaranteed execution order with run, if, and transitions.
optionC: Declarative instructions only work in Canvas View for visual editing, while procedural instructions require Script View and cannot be represented in the visual interface.
explanation:
Declarative instructions providing conversational flexibility through LLM interpretation, while procedural instructions use the -> prefix to guarantee execution order with run, if and transitions, is the differentiation. Agent Script's language page says logic instructions (->) "run deterministically every time", and the actions reference says an action called with run in the logic "is run every time the subagent is run".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (declarative needs Flow; procedural can't reach external systems) — procedural logic runs actions, and actions can call flows, Apex and APIs.
Option C (declarative only in Canvas, procedural only in Script) — both views represent the same script.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-lang.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-actions.html

question: When is the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol an appropriate communication choice?
optionA: When agents need to invoke third-party API
optionB: When agents need to access tools
optionC: When agents need to collaborate
explanation:
When agents need to collaborate is when A2A fits. Salesforce's integration-pattern guidance says Agent2Agent integration "allows you to distribute the workload across a team of specialized agents" through task delegation between agents.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (to invoke a third-party API) — a direct API call or MCP.
Option B (to access tools) — tool access is what MCP standardizes.
References:
https://www.salesforce.com/blog/how-to-choose-integration-pattern-for-agentforce/
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005317683&language=en_US&type=1

question: What happens when a chunk of text is vectorized?
optionA: It creates numerical representations of chunk content to enable meaning-based retrieval.
optionB: It encrypts the content so it can be stored securely within Data 360 data spaces.
optionC: It reduces the file size of the original document to reduce Data 360 costs.
explanation:
Vectorizing creates numerical representations of the chunk's content to enable meaning-based retrieval. Salesforce's Chunk Data page says "Data 360 turns those chunks into machine-readable vector embeddings", and the max-token page describes the embedding algorithm converting "each chunk into a vector".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (encrypts the content) — an embedding is a representation for similarity search, not encryption.
Option C (reduces file size to cut cost) — the original content is kept; embeddings are stored alongside it.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_search_index_grounding.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_search_index_max_token_setting.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has a strict change management process that requires all possible configuration to be completed in a sandbox which will be deployed to production. The Agentforce Specialist is tasked with setting up Work Summaries for Enhanced Messaging. Einstein Generative AI is already enabled in production, and the Einstein Work Summaries permission set is already available in production. Which other configuration steps should the Agentforce Specialist take in the sandbox that can be deployed to the production org?
optionA: Create custom fields to store Issue, Resolution, and Summary; create a Quick Action that updates these fields; add the Wrap Up component to the Messaging Session record page layout; and create Permission Set Assignments for the intended agents.
optionB: From the Einstein setup menu, select Turn on Einstein; create custom fields to store Issue, Resolution, and Summary; create a Quick Action that updates these fields; and add the Wrap Up component to the Messaging Session record page layout.
optionC: Create custom fields to store Issue, Resolution, and Summary; create a Quick Action that updates these fields; and add the Wrap Up component to the Messaging Session record page layout.
explanation:
Creating the Issue, Resolution and Summary fields, the Quick Action that updates them, and adding the Wrap Up component to the Messaging Session record page are the steps that can be built in a sandbox and deployed — all metadata. Work Summaries itself is turned on per channel and reps get a permission set, which happen in production.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (also creates permission set assignments) — assignments are user data, not deployable metadata, and have to be made in production.
Option B (also turns on Einstein from setup) — an org setting that is already on in production and does not travel in a deployment.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=service.cc_generative_ai_work_summaries.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers would like to route a service agent conversation to a human agent queue. Which tool connects the service agent to the human agent queue for escalation?
optionA: Outbound Omni-Channel Flow
optionB: Screen Flow
optionC: Prompt Flow
explanation:
An outbound Omni-Channel flow connects the service agent to the human queue. Salesforce's Transfer Conversations from an Agent with an Omni-Channel Flow says that on messaging channels "service agents transfer conversations to a specified destination, such as a rep or queue, using an outbound Omni-Channel flow", which you create, activate and add to the agent's Messaging connection as its escalation.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Screen Flow) — collects input from a user on screen; it does not route work.
Option C (Prompt Flow) — a template-triggered flow that feeds data into a prompt template, not a routing tool.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.service_agent_escalation.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer is authenticated and identified as being either bronze, silver, or gold membership level. Those levels define which subagents or actions are available to the agent to perform specific tasks as per the level-based entitlements. What is the best way to ensure the agent responds appropriately?
optionA: Use before reasoning to set custom variables that will be used in filters and flow logic.
optionB: Use after reasoning to set custom variables that will be used in filters and flow logic.
optionC: Use Agent Router to set custom variables that will be used in filters and flow logic.
explanation:
Using before reasoning to set the custom variables that filters and flow logic depend on is the exam's answer: before_reasoning is "functionally equivalent to adding logic to the beginning of a subagent's instructions", so the membership tier is in place before the LLM sees which tools are available, and available when filters then hide what a bronze member may not use. Be aware that option C is also documented. Agent Script's Flow of Control page says "You typically use the start_agent subagent to set the initial value of variables", and subagent-level filters are evaluated in that router — so the Agent Router is an equally valid place to set entitlement variables, particularly for filtering whole subagents.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (after reasoning) — runs after the reasoning loop exits, too late to shape what the LLM could choose on that turn.
Option C (Agent Router) — not wrong on the documentation, as noted above; the exam keys before reasoning.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-before-after-reasoning.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-flow.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-patterns-filtering.html

corrected.note: Kept as the exam key, but option C is also documented: Agent Script's Flow of Control page says "You typically use the start_agent subagent to set the initial value of variables", and subagent filters are evaluated in that router. Before reasoning and the router are both valid places to set entitlement variables, so the item has two defensible answers.

question: Universal Containers (UC) is using Einstein Generative AI to generate an account summary. UC aims to ensure the content is safe and inclusive, utilizing the Einstein Trust Layer's toxicity scoring to assess the content's safety level. In the Einstein Generative AI Toxicity Scoring system, what does a toxicity category score of 1 indicate?
optionA: The response is the least toxic.
optionB: The response is not toxic.
optionC: The response is the most toxic.
explanation:
A toxicity category score of 1 means the response is the most toxic. Salesforce's Review Toxicity Scores page says scores for toxicity categories such as hate and violence "range from 0 through 1, with 1 being the most toxic". Note the one category that runs the other way: the safety score also ranges from 0 to 1 but "with 1 being the safest", and 0.5 or above counts as safe.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (least toxic) — the scale is reversed for toxicity categories; 1 is the most toxic.
Option B (not toxic) — confuses a category score with the safety score, where 1 is safest.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_audit_toxicity.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) has configured an Agentforce Data Library using Knowledge articles. When testing in Agent Builder and the Experience Cloud site, the agent is not responding with grounded Knowledge article information. However, when tested in Prompt Builder, the response returns correctly. What should UC do to troubleshoot the issue?
optionA: Create a new permission set that assigns "Manage Knowledge" and assign it to the Agentforce Service Agent User.
optionB: Ensure the assigned User permission set includes access to the prompt template used to access the Knowledge articles.
optionC: Ensure the Data Cloud User permission set has been assigned to the Agentforce Service Agent User.
explanation:
Ensuring the Data Cloud User permission set is assigned to the Agentforce Service Agent user is the fix. Salesforce's Agentforce Data Library Troubleshooting page says "To access the retriever and default data space assign the Data Cloud User", and adds that the default data space must be added to that permission set — Prompt Builder worked because it ran as the admin, who already had that access.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Manage Knowledge for the agent user) — authoring permission; retrieval needs Data 360 access, not Knowledge management.
Option B (access to the prompt template) — the Answer Questions with Knowledge action uses the library's retriever; template access is not the missing piece.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_troubleshooting.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Northern Trail Outfitters is testing an agent connected to an Agentforce Data Library. The agent successfully retrieves the correct data from the library, but delivers the response to the user as raw JSON structures instead of grammatically correct conversational language. Which quality evaluation scores poorly in this scenario?
optionA: Coherence
optionB: Conciseness
optionC: Completeness
explanation:
Coherence scores poorly. Testing Center's Choose Evaluations page defines Coherence as assessing "if the response was transformed into grammatically correct, conversational language. For example, if information has been taken from Salesforce objects and delivered as raw data like JSON structures" — this exact scenario.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Conciseness) — evaluates whether the response is short but accurate; length is not the problem here.
Option C (Completeness) — checks whether all expected information is present, and the data was retrieved correctly.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center_evaluations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Specialist implements Einstein Sales Emails for a sales team. The team wants to send personalized follow-up emails to leads based on their interactions and data stored in Salesforce. The Agentforce Specialist needs to configure the system to use the most accurate and up-to-date information for email generation. Which grounding technique should the Agentforce Specialist use?
optionA: Ground with Apex Merge Fields
optionB: Ground with Record Merge Fields
optionC: Automatic grounding using Draft with Einstein feature
explanation:
Grounding with Record Merge Fields is the technique, because the team wants the follow-up to use each lead's interactions and current record data. Salesforce's Understand How Einstein Generative AI Creates Sales Emails shows that the standard, automatic grounding behind Draft with Einstein uses a fixed set of fields — the recipient's name, title, company and industry and the sender's name and company. A custom Sales Email prompt template grounded with record merge fields pulls whichever fields the follow-up needs, live from the record when the email is drafted.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Apex merge fields) — needed only when the data requires code, such as a query or external API; record data is reached directly with record merge fields.
Option C (automatic grounding with Draft with Einstein) — works, but only with the fixed standard fields, which do not include the lead's interaction history.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.einstein_sales_emails_overview.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.einstein_sales_emails_considerations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed automatic grounding with Draft with Einstein, while its own explanation argued for Record Merge Fields. Standard Sales Emails grounding uses a fixed set of fields (contact or lead name, title, company, industry and the sender), per Understand How Einstein Generative AI Creates Sales Emails; follow-ups based on a lead's interactions and other current record data need a Sales Email template grounded with record merge fields.

question: Universal Containers has been building an agent using Canvas. It has created an "Issue Refund" action. Business rules dictate that refunds can only be issued if the customer's Account Tier is "Platinum." Currently, the agent relies on its system instructions to check the tier, but it occasionally hallucinates authorization and attempts to call the refund action for Standard customers, resulting in backend errors. How should the Agentforce Specialist use filters to deterministically ensure the agent cannot process the "Issue Refund" action unless the customer meets the criteria?
optionA: Update the agent's system instructions with a strict rule to manually filter out any refund requests if the customer's account tier is not Platinum.
optionB: Apply a text filter to the Agent Session that automatically blocks the word "refund" from the user's prompt unless they are a Platinum customer.
optionC: Configure an Action Condition filter on the "Issue Refund"action so that it is only available to the agent when Account Tier equals"Platinum."
explanation:
Configuring a condition filter on the "Issue Refund" action, so it is only available when Account Tier equals "Platinum", is the deterministic fix. Salesforce's filtering pattern says filters control which actions are available, and "If the conditions aren't met, the LLM can't access the subagent or reasoning action"; its first tip is to "Protect against customer manipulation: Filter business-sensitive features. Don't only rely on prompt engineering."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a stricter rule in the system instructions) — still prompt engineering, which is what is already failing.
Option B (a text filter blocking the word "refund") — blocks a word, not the action, and would stop Platinum customers from asking too.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-patterns-filtering.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-tools.html

question: Universal Containers is building a custom agent and creating a new Apex action that accepts a collection of text values, such as a list of product names, as an input parameter. The Agentforce Specialist is configuring the action's metadata in Agentforce Assets and needs to properly map this input so the reasoning engine can pass the list of strings correctly. When defining this input, which complex_data_type_name should the Agentforce Specialist use?
optionA: lightning__stringType
optionB: apex__String
optionC: lightning__textType
explanation:
lightning__stringType is the Lightning type for string values. Salesforce's Lightning Types in Agent Action page says Apex inputs like "dates, strings, and numbers" are mapped to standard Lightning types "such as lightning__dateType, lightning__stringType, and lightning__numberType", and the Agent Script actions reference uses complex_data_type_name to name the Lightning type a parameter carries.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (apex__String) — names the Apex implementation type, not a Lightning type the reasoning engine understands.
Option C (lightning__textType) — not among the documented standard types for string values.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/lightning-types-standard.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-actions.html

question: Universal Containers recently launched a pilot program to integrate conversational AI into its CRM business operations with Agentforce Agents. How should the Agentforce Specialist monitor Agents' usability and the assignment of actions?
optionA: Run a report on the Platform Debug Logs.
optionB: Query the Agent log data using the Metadata API.
optionC: Run Agent Analytics.
explanation:
Running Agent Analytics is how to monitor usability and action assignment. Salesforce describes Agentforce Observability's analytics as a way to "Understand usage, effectiveness, and feedback insights of all Agentforce agents" and to "manage ineffective topics or actions", with out-of-the-box dashboards.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (reports on Platform Debug Logs) — debug logs trace code execution; they are not agent usage analytics.
Option B (query agent logs with the Metadata API) — the Metadata API moves configuration, not session data.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005226932&language=en_US&type=1
https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/observability/

question: Universal Containers (UC) has a new AI project. What should UC consider when adding a related list on the Account page to be used in the prompt template?
optionA: Prompt Builder must be used to assign the fields from the related list as a JSON format.
optionB: After selecting a related list from the Account, use the field picker to choose merge fields in Prompt Builder.
optionC: The fields for the related list are based on the default page layout of the Account for the current user.
explanation:
The related list's fields being based on the Account page layout for the current user is the consideration. Grounding with Related List Merge Fields says "the fields for the related list are based on the page layout of the parent object for the current user", so two users with different layouts can ground the same template with different fields.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (assign the fields as JSON in Prompt Builder) — nothing to assign; the retrieved data is rendered in JSON automatically.
Option B (pick merge fields with the field picker after selecting the list) — the related list merges as a whole; its fields come from the page layout, not from a picker.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_ground_related_list.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers plans to enable Agentforce in Slack so teams can interact with agents directly in Slack channels. Which description represents the key steps required to enable Agentforce in Slack?
optionA: Enable the default Slack channel Agentforce, and assign Slack agent access to users.
optionB: Configure the Slack workflow to invoke the Agentforce API, enabling users to interact with agents through predefined triggers and automated steps.
optionC: Configure the Slack agent connection and, in Manage Agentforce, install the agent, then assign agent access to users.
explanation:
Configuring the Slack agent connection, installing the agent from Manage Agentforce, then giving users access is the sequence. Salesforce's Connect an Agent to Slack says to add the Slack connection to the agent, "Give your users access to your agent and then activate it", and in a Pro or Business+ workspace go to Admin, "select Manage Agentforce", review the agent and click "Install agent".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (enable a default "Agentforce" Slack channel) — no default channel exists; the agent is connected and installed.
Option B (a Slack workflow calling the Agentforce API) — a custom build around the API, not how Agentforce is enabled in Slack.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_deploy_emp_slack.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers' Service Agent executes a flow action to retrieve Opportunity records. The Opportunity object has an organization-wide default of Private. The agent returns no results despite matching records existing and the flow logic being correctly configured. Which resolution strictly adheres to the principle of least privilege?
optionA: Add the required object permissions to the Einstein Service Agent User's permission set and configure appropriate sharing rules
optionB: Set the agent action flow to run in System Mode without sharing
optionC: Change the Opportunity object's organization-wide default to Public Read Only so the Einstein Service Agent User can access records
explanation:
Adding the required object permissions to the agent user's permission set and configuring appropriate sharing rules is the least-privilege fix. Salesforce's Configure Service Agent Access says the agent user starts with minimal access that you expand "based on the principle of least privilege", and that record visibility comes from the agent user's permissions, field-level security and sharing — "Roles grant users record access via sharing rules and role hierarchy".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (run the flow in system mode without sharing) — bypasses record security entirely.
Option C (change the Opportunity default to Public Read Only) — opens every opportunity to every internal user to fix one agent.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_user.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Coral Cloud Resorts (CCR) sees the agent forgot the dietary/activity preferences gathered earlier. They need those preferences to persist throughout the session. What should CCR implement?
optionA: Configure custom variables to capture/store customer preferences from action outputs.
optionB: Rely on natural conversation memory and instruct the agent to look back.
optionC: Create a context variable to capture/store customer preferences as action outputs.
explanation:
Configuring custom variables to capture and store customer preferences from action outputs is what makes them persist. Salesforce's developer blog on Agentforce variables distinguishes "Context variable: These are system generated variables holding information about the user and the conversation sessions" from "Custom variables: These can be instantiated by the user", and says variables "can be used as both input and output for actions" and provide "persistent storage for critical information" for the whole conversation.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (rely on conversation memory and tell the agent to look back) — the unstructured memory that already forgot the preferences.
Option C (a context variable fed from action outputs) — context variables are system-generated from the session (for example, Messaging Session fields); they are not what you create to hold action outputs.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2025/04/agentforce-variables-a-new-way-to-structure-agent-memory
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-variables.html

corrected.note: The dump keyed context variables. Salesforce defines context variables as "system generated variables holding information about the user and the conversation sessions" and custom variables as the ones you create, which "can be used as both input and output for actions" (Agentforce Variables, Salesforce Developers Blog). Preferences gathered from action outputs belong in custom variables. The dump's explanation quoted a "Session Memory and Context Management Guide" that does not exist.

question: Universal Containers is considering leveraging the Einstein Trust Layer in conjunction with Einstein Generative AI Audit Data. Which audit data is available using the Einstein Trust Layer?
optionA: Response accuracy and offensiveness score
optionB: Hallucination score and bias score
optionC: Masked data and toxicity score
explanation:
Masked data and toxicity scores are the Trust Layer audit data. Salesforce's Audit Trail page says generative AI audit data "includes data about the Einstein Trust Layer features such as data masking and toxicity scores".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (accuracy and offensiveness scores) — not audit fields; the Trust Layer scores toxicity categories.
Option B (hallucination and bias scores) — not produced by the Trust Layer audit trail.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_audit_trail.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_audit_toxicity.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator at Universal Containers has successfully deployed a new agent from a sandbox to production using a change set. The agent uses a prompt template that invokes a Salesforce flow to perform a complex calculation. In production, when users interact with the agent, it fails with an error message every time the flow is supposed to run. The flow was included in the change set and is present in production. What is the most likely cause of this issue?
optionA: The flow was not manually activated in the production org after the deployment.
optionB: The user in production does not have permission to run the flow.
optionC: The change set did not include the dependent Apex classes for the flow.
explanation:
The flow not being activated in production after the deployment is the most likely cause. Salesforce's Deploy Processes and Flows as Active page says "By default, processes and flows that are active in a sandbox or non-production org are deployed to a production org as inactive. After deployment, manually reactivate the new versions" — unless the org has turned on the setting to deploy them as active.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (the user lacks permission to run the flow) — would fail for that user, and an inactive flow fails for everyone, which fits "every time".
Option C (missing dependent Apex classes) — a change set with missing dependencies fails to deploy; this one deployed successfully.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_distribute_deploy_active.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) needs to create a custom prompt template that can be called from a Lightning web component. Which prompt template type should UC create?
optionA: Field Generation
optionB: Sales Email
optionC: Flex
explanation:
A Flex template is the type for a custom Lightning web component. Salesforce's Prompt Template Types describes Flex as "Content for any business purposes that other templates don't cover. Flex prompt templates let you define your own resources", and a Flex template can be invoked from Apex behind the component, whose response the LWC then displays.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Field Generation) — runs from a button next to a record field and writes into that field.
Option B (Sales Email) — runs in the email composer.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_template_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2024/04/invoke-prompt-templates-from-flow-apex-or-the-rest-api

question: Universal Containers (UC) has a legacy system that needs to integrate with Salesforce. UC wishes to create a digest of account action plans using the generative API feature. Which API service should UC use to meet this requirement?
optionA: REST API
optionB: Metadata API
optionC: SOAP API
explanation:
The REST API is the service. Salesforce's developer blog on invoking prompt templates says "Thanks to the Connect REST API, it's not only possible to invoke prompt templates programmatically within the Salesforce Platform, but also from third-party systems" — the prompt template generations resource returns the resolved prompt and the generated response.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Metadata API) — moves configuration between orgs; it does not run a prompt.
Option C (SOAP API) — has no generative endpoint for prompt templates.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/blogs/2024/04/invoke-prompt-templates-from-flow-apex-or-the-rest-api

question: Universal Containers (UC) uses a file upload-based data library and custom prompt to support AI-driven training content. However, users report that the AI frequently returns outdated documents. Which corrective action should UC implement to improve content relevancy?
optionA: Switch the data library source from file uploads to a Knowledge-based data library, because Salesforce Knowledge bases automatically manage document recency, ensuring current documents are returned.
optionB: Configure a custom retriever that includes a filter condition limiting retrieval to documents updated within a defined recent period, ensuring that only current content is used for AI responses.
optionC: Continue using the default retriever without filters, because periodic re-uploads will eventually phase out outdated documents without further configuration or the need for custom retrievers.
explanation:
Configuring a custom retriever with a filter that limits retrieval to recently updated documents is the corrective action. Salesforce's Retrieve Data page says individual retrievers "can return content that's filtered based on a category of articles or the most recent information (such as the last 90 days)", with up to 10 filter conditions on fields the search index exposes.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (switch to a Knowledge-based library) — would fix recency, but the training content is files, not Knowledge articles; the filter fixes the library UC actually has.
Option C (keep the default retriever and re-upload over time) — outdated files stay indexed until removed.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_create.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers is testing an agent with a "Reset Password" action restricted by the guard available when @variables.isVerified == True. During a single conversation turn, the large language model successfully sets the isVerified flag to true using @utils.setVariables, but fails to invoke the "Reset Password" action immediately afterward. What must the Agentforce Specialist consider regarding how the reasoning engine evaluates action availability?
optionA: The action is available from the start; the reasoning engine's intent to solve the user's issue automatically overrides the available when guard.
optionB: The action becomes available immediately; available when conditions dynamically re-evaluate after every variable change within a single turn.
