optionC: The action remains unavailable for that turn; available when conditions control action visibility to the LLM and evaluate before the reasoning cycle begins, so the action will not be callable until the next turn.
explanation:
The action remaining unavailable for that turn, because available when is evaluated when the tools are handed to the LLM, is the consideration. Salesforce's Agent Script reference says Agentforce passes the tools in reasoning.actions to the LLM "after parsing the entire subagent", and available when decides which tools are included. A flag the LLM sets partway through that reasoning does not re-parse the subagent, so the guarded action becomes visible on a later pass. The documentation does not spell out the within-turn timing in so many words; the reference is the parse-then-reason order it describes.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the action is available from the start; intent overrides the guard) — the point of available when is that the LLM cannot override it.
Option B (conditions re-evaluate after every variable change in the turn) — the reference describes the tool list being built when the subagent is parsed, not rebuilt on each variable change.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-actions.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-flow.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-tools.html

question: Global Finance Corp (GFC) is expanding its Agentforce rollout from a basic customer service agent to a suite of specialized agents handling Fraud Detection, Loan Origination, and Billing. GFC operates entirely within a single, global Salesforce instance. The CIO wants to ensure that as the number of specialized agents scales, the company maintains strict, centralized control over security guardrails and user context, ensuring customers do not have to repeat themselves when their request spans multiple departments. What is a reasonable architectural approach to achieve this level of scalability and control?
optionA: Use the Model Context Protocol (MCP) to federate multiple external, third-party agents directly into the existing Agentforce Service console.
optionB: Implement a Multi-Org, Multi-Agent (MOMA) architecture connected via the Agent-to-Agent (A2A) protocol to safely isolate each department's agent.
optionC: Deploy a Single-Org, Multi-Agent (SOMA) architecture using a primary Orchestrator agent to manage shared context natively and route subtasks to the specialized agents.
explanation:
A Single-Org, Multi-Agent (SOMA) architecture with a primary orchestrator agent is the reasonable approach. Salesforce's knowledge article on SOMA and MCP separates architectures — "SOMA and MOMA as where agents live" — from protocols, "MCP and A2A as how they talk". GFC runs in one Salesforce instance, so its specialized agents can share user context and one set of guardrails inside that org, with an orchestrator routing subtasks.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (MCP to federate third-party agents into the console) — MCP connects agents to tools, not agents to each other, and nothing here is third-party.
Option B (Multi-Org, Multi-Agent over A2A) — built for agents spread across orgs or vendors; splitting one instance into isolated agents gives up the shared context the CIO wants.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005317683&language=en_US&type=1

question: Universal Containers (UC) uses Salesforce Service Cloud to support its customers and agents handling cases. UC is considering implementing Agentforce and extending Service Cloud to mobile users. When would Agentforce implementation be most advantageous?
optionA: When the goal is to streamline customer support processes and improve response times
optionB: When the main objective is to enhance data security and compliance measures
optionC: When the focus is on optimizing marketing campaigns and strategies
explanation:
When the goal is to streamline customer support processes and improve response times is when Agentforce pays off in Service Cloud. Salesforce's agent types describe the Service Agent as one that "Intelligently supports your customers with common inquiries and escalates complex issues" and the Service Assistant as helping reps "resolve cases faster with case summaries and step-by-step resolution guidance" — both about support speed.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (enhance data security and compliance) — Agentforce inherits Salesforce's security model; improving security is not its purpose.
Option C (optimize marketing campaigns) — a Marketing Cloud concern, not a Service Cloud rollout.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_setup_explore_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What is an Agentforce Specialist able to do when the "Enrich event logs with conversation data" setting in Agentforce is enabled?
optionA: View the user click path that led to each copilot action.
optionB: View session data including user input and copilot responses for sessions over the past 7 days.
optionC: Generate detailed reports on all Copilot conversations over any time period.
explanation:
Viewing session data, including user input and agent responses, for the past 7 days is what the setting adds. Salesforce's Enable Enhanced Event Logs (the current name of the setting) says that without it, message events are logged "but the messages themselves aren't included", that enabling it lets you "view user messages as well as agent messages and events", and that "Event logs store information for seven days".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the click path to each action) — event logs record session events and messages, not UI click paths.
Option C (reports over any time period) — the logs keep only seven days.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_setup_enhanced_event_logs.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has an active standard email prompt template that does not fully deliver on the business requirements. Which steps should an Agentforce Specialist take to use the content of the standard prompt email template in question and customize it to fully meet the business requirements?
optionA: Save as New Template and edit as needed.
optionB: Clone the existing template and modify as needed.
optionC: Save as New Version and edit as needed.
explanation:
Save as New Template and edit it is the way to reuse a standard email template's content and customize it. Prompt Builder's Save As menu offers "Save as a New Template", which turns the current template into a new custom template with any unsaved changes, and Override a Standard Prompt Template says that "If a standard template isn't overridable, you can instead copy it and create a custom template."
Be aware of the nuance: some standard templates are overridable, and for those Salesforce documents Save As, then Save as a New Version (option C), which, once activated, "takes the place of the standard version". So C is also right for an overridable template; A works for every standard template.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Clone the existing template) — Prompt Builder has no Clone action; copying is done through Save As.
Option C (Save as New Version) — right only when the standard template is overridable, as described above.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_override_standard_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_use_multiple_versions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

corrected.note: The dump keyed Clone the existing template, which is not a Prompt Builder action; its explanation also claimed there is no Save as New Template option, which Use Multiple Versions of a Prompt Template contradicts ("Save As | Save as a New Template"). Override a Standard Prompt Template adds a nuance: an overridable standard template is customized with Save as a New Version (option C), and one that is not overridable is copied into a custom template. Save as New Template is kept as the answer that works for any standard template.

question: Universal Containers (UC) users are complaining that agent answers are not satisfactory. The agent is using PDF files as a knowledge source. How should UC troubleshoot this issue?
optionA: Analyze the data mapping between source fields and Data Cloud object fields.
optionB: Check that the agent has the PDF file field permission access for the data library.
optionC: Verify the retriever's filter criteria and data source connection.
explanation:
Verifying the retriever's filter criteria and its data source connection is where to start. A file-based data library answers through a search index and retriever, and Salesforce's Retrieve Data page notes that retriever filters narrow what is returned — a filter that excludes the right PDFs, or an index that never finished building from its source, produces exactly these unsatisfying answers.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (mapping between source fields and Data Cloud fields) — uploaded PDFs are chunked by the library; there is no field mapping to tune.
Option B (a PDF file field permission for the agent) — no such permission exists for data library files.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_about.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_ai_retriever_create.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Specialist is setting up Salesforce Knowledge as the data source for a Data Library and must select "Identifying Fields" to help Agentforce locate the right information. The Knowledge article contents are rich, detailed, and quite long. What should the Agentforce Specialist use as Identifying Fields?
optionA: The main contents of the article to ensure the most relevant article is used.
optionB: Any text or text area fields that provide a concise summary of the article.
optionC: Any standard or custom formula field that contains a suitable concatenated key.
explanation:
Any text or text area fields that give a concise summary of the article are the identifying fields to use. Salesforce's Use Salesforce Knowledge page says identifying fields "must be a text or text area type fields and are limited to 512 tokens" and recommends "fields that include a concise outline of the associated knowledge article", with the long body selected as content fields instead.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the main article contents) — the long body exceeds the 512-token limit and belongs in content fields.
Option C (a formula field with a concatenated key) — Knowledge data libraries support only text and text area fields.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_select_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A customer wants to analyze complete agent interactions, from the initial user request through to the final resolution, to better understand agent behavior and response quality. Which Agentforce feature should an Agentforce Specialist recommend?
optionA: Agent Inspection
optionB: Agent Insights
optionC: Agent Optimization
explanation:
Agent Inspection is the feature for examining complete interactions. Salesforce's Agentforce Observability lists "Agent Configuration and Inspection" among its capabilities, alongside analytics, health monitoring and session tracing, and describes the ability to "Investigate Specific Interactions" with "a full session trace", drilling to the conversation level "to review where and why the agent struggled".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Agent Insights) — aggregate usage and effectiveness insights, not a turn-by-turn look at one interaction.
Option C (Agent Optimization) — acts on patterns such as ineffective subagents or actions; it is not the end-to-end inspection view.
References:
https://www.salesforce.com/agentforce/observability/
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005226932&language=en_US&type=1

question: The sales team at a hotel resort would like to generate a guest summary about the guests' interests and provide recommendations based on their activity preferences captured in each guest profile. They want the summary to be available only on the contact record page. Which AI capability should the team use?
optionA: Flow Builder
optionB: Agentforce Builder
optionC: Prompt Builder
explanation:
Prompt Builder is the capability, because the output is generated text — a guest summary with recommendations — shown only on the contact record page. A prompt template grounded on the guest's profile fields produces it; Prompt Builder's template types include ones that summarize records and fill record fields in Lightning Experience.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Flow Builder) — automates logic; generating the summary text still needs a prompt template.
Option B (Agentforce Builder) — builds conversational agents that act across many contexts, which is more than a single summary on one page needs.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_standard_template_types.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: How does Secure Data Retrieval ensure that only authorized users can access necessary Salesforce data for dynamic grounding?
optionA: Retrieves Salesforce data based on the 'Run As" users permissions.
optionB: Retrieves Salesforce data based on the user's permissions executing the prompt.
optionC: Retrieves Salesforces data based on the Prompt template's object permissions.
explanation:
Retrieving data based on the permissions of the user executing the prompt is how Secure Data Retrieval works. Salesforce's Einstein Trust Layer page says "Data retrieval for grounding the prompt is based on the permissions of the user executing the prompt" and "preserves in place all standard Salesforce role-based controls for user permissions and field-level security".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (the "Run As" user's permissions) — retrieval runs as the executing user, not a substitute.
Option C (the prompt template's object permissions) — templates have no permissions of their own.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_trust_arch.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What is the correct process to leverage Prompt Builder in a Salesforce org?
optionA: Select the appropriate prompt template type to use, select one of Salesforce's standard prompts, determine the object to associate the prompt, select a record to validate against, and associate the prompt to an action.
optionB: Select the appropriate prompt template type to use, develop the prompt within the prompt workspace, select resources to dynamically insert CRM-derived grounding data, pick the model to use, and test and validate the generated responses.
optionC: Enable the target object for generative prompting, develop the prompt within the prompt workspace, select records to fine-tune and ground the response, enable the Trust Layer, and associate the prompt to an action.
explanation:
Selecting the template type, developing the prompt in the workspace, inserting resources for CRM grounding data, picking the model and testing the responses is the process. It follows Prompt Builder's own flow: create a template of a type, draft it in the Prompt Template Workspace, add grounding through merge fields and resources, choose a model configuration, and preview against a record before activating.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (select a standard prompt as the base) — custom templates are written in the workspace; starting from a standard template is only one option and skips grounding and model choice.
Option C (enable the object, fine-tune with records, enable the Trust Layer) — no per-object enablement or record fine-tuning step exists, and the Trust Layer is not switched on per template.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_use_multiple_versions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_template_ingredients.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) plans to implement prompt templates that utilize the standard foundation models. What should UC consider when building prompt templates in Prompt Builder?
optionA: Include multiple-choice questions within the prompt to test the LLM's understanding of the context.
optionB: Ask it to role-play as a character in the prompt template to provide more context to the LLM.
optionC: Train LLM with data using different writing styles including word choice, intensifiers, emojis, and punctuation.
explanation:
Asking the model to role-play as a character to provide more context is the consideration. Salesforce's Best Practices for Building Prompt Templates says "To give the LLM more contextual information, ask it to role play as a character, such as a sales or support representative. Then define the character's goal."
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (multiple-choice questions to test the LLM) — adds noise to the prompt rather than context.
Option C (train the LLM on different writing styles) — standard foundation models are not trained from Prompt Builder; the guidance is to choose one style and use it consistently in the template.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator wants to check the response of the Flex prompt template they've built, but the preview button is greyed out. What is the reason for this?
optionA: The records related to the prompt have not been selected.
optionB: The prompt has not been saved and activated.
optionC: A merge field has not been inserted in the prompt.
explanation:
The related records not being selected is why preview is unavailable. Salesforce's Create a Flex Prompt Template says that to preview, "In Preview Settings, select an object for each resource" and then "Click Save & Preview" — a Flex template defines its own inputs, and Prompt Builder cannot resolve them until a record is chosen for each.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (the prompt isn't saved and activated) — preview is used while drafting; activation is not required.
Option C (no merge field inserted) — a template without merge fields can still be previewed; the missing piece is the input records.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_create_flex_prompt_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An administrator at Universal Containers is setting up a new Sales Development Representative (SDR) Agent. The agent's purpose is to nurture cold leads before connecting them to the assigned sales rep. To ensure the agent has all the necessary access to the leads in the North America sales region, what should the administrator do?
optionA: Assign the user in the highest-level role within the North America role hierarchy as the SDR Agent User.
optionB: Grant View All record permission of the Lead object to the 'Einstein Agent User' profile.
optionC: Create a criteria-based sharing rule to grant access to targeted lead records to SDR Agent User.
explanation:
Creating a criteria-based sharing rule that grants the SDR agent user access to the targeted leads is the approach. The agent's permission set grants Lead object access (Read and Edit on Lead), but record visibility still comes from sharing, and Salesforce's guidance for agent users is to expand access "based on the principle of least privilege" — a rule scoped to North America leads does that.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (make the agent user the highest-role user in the region) — the agent needs its own dedicated user, and borrowing a senior role grants far more than the leads.
Option B (View All on Lead for the Einstein Agent User profile) — every lead in the org, the opposite of least privilege.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.sales_agent_sdr_permissions.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_user.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Coral Cloud Resorts wants visibility into credit usage associated with testing. Which feature supports this?
optionA: Agentforce Analytics
optionB: Digital Wallet
optionC: Testing Center
explanation:
Digital Wallet is the feature for visibility into credit usage. The credit usage that remains shows up in Digital Wallet.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Agentforce Analytics) — reports on agent usage and effectiveness, not on credit consumption.
Option C (Testing Center) — shows test results and scores; its documentation does not describe a credit-usage view.

question: What is the main benefit of using a Knowledge article in an Agentforce Data Library?
optionA: Only the retriever for Knowledge articles allows for agents to access Knowledge from both inside the platform and on a customer's website.
optionB: It provides a structured, searchable repository of approved documents so the agent can retrieve reliable information for each inquiry..
optionC: The retriever for Knowledge articles has better accuracy and performance than the default retriever.
explanation:
A structured, searchable repository of approved content the agent can retrieve reliably is the main benefit. A Knowledge-based data library indexes only published articles ("Only published articles are considered for the data library") into a search index and retriever used by the Answer Questions with Knowledge action.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (only Knowledge retrievers reach both the platform and a website) — any data library serves whichever agents and channels it is assigned to.
Option C (a Knowledge retriever outperforms the default retriever) — the library creates its own retriever either way; there is no documented accuracy advantage.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_select_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_setup.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Specialist is tasked to optimize a business process flow by assigning actions to agents within the Salesforce Agentforce Platform. What is the correct method for the Agentforce Specialist to assign actions to an Agent?
optionA: Assign the action to a Topic First in Agent Builder.
optionB: Assign the action to a Topic first on the Agent Actions detail page.
optionC: Assign the action to a Topic first on Action Builder.
explanation:
Assigning the action to a topic (now called a subagent) first in Agent Builder is the method. Agents reach actions through their subagents: the reasoning engine classifies a request into a subagent and then chooses among that subagent's actions, and actions are added to subagents in Agentforce Builder.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (on the Agent Actions detail page) — where an action is defined, not where it is assigned.
Option C (in Action Builder) — not a separate place where actions are assigned to agents.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_custom.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_parent_deploy.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A company built a custom Apex action invoked by an Employee Agent to fetch data from an external API. The callout method uses the current user's Salesforce session ID to authenticate the callout. The external callout works perfectly in the UI, but silently fails when the agent triggers it. What is the architectural best practice to fix this?
optionA: Explicitly extend the Apex class security to the logged-in user's profile.
optionB: Ensure the Employee Agent is assigned the Agentforce Service Agent User permission set group.
optionC: Replace the session ID retrieval with a Named Credential.
explanation:
Replacing the session ID with a Named Credential is the architectural fix. When the agent runs the action, there is no interactive UI session whose ID can authenticate the callout, so session-based authentication fails. Salesforce's Apex guide documents Named Credentials as the way to specify a callout endpoint and its authentication in one definition, so the code never handles a session ID.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (extend Apex class security to the user's profile) — class access is not the problem; the callout's authentication is.
Option B (assign the Agentforce Service Agent User permission set group) — that group is for the service agent user, not an Employee Agent, and grants no external authentication.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_callouts_named_credentials.htm

question: Universal Containers is interested in using Call Explorer to quickly gain insights from meetings recorded by its sales team. What should the Agentforce Specialist be aware of before enabling this feature?
optionA: Call Explorer operates independently of Salesforce Knowledge, requiring no prior setup.
optionB: Custom Call Explorer actions need to be built before it can be configured.
optionC: Call Explorer requires the Einstein Conversation Insights permission set to be enabled.
explanation:
Call Explorer requiring Einstein Conversation Insights permission sets to be assigned is the thing to know. Call Explorer is part of Einstein Conversation Insights, and Salesforce's setup guide says to "Connect a recording provider, assign permission sets, and define insights" before calls are processed.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (it operates independently with no setup) — needs ECI enabled, a recording provider and permission sets.
Option B (custom Call Explorer actions must be built first) — no custom actions are needed.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.call_coaching_setup.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers deployed the new Agentforce Sales Development Representative (SDR) into production, but sales reps are saying they can't find it. What is causing this issue?
optionA: Sales rep users profiles are missing the Allow SDR Agent permission.
optionB: Sales rep users do not have access to the SDR Agent object.
optionC: Sales rep users are missing the Use SDR Agent permission set.
explanation:
The sales reps missing the Use SDR Agent permission set is the cause. Salesforce has since renamed the agent Agentforce Engagement (it was Lead Nurturing, and SDR before that), and its permission-set page says "The Use Engagement Agent permission set allows human users to access and interact with Agentforce Engagement" — the same set under its current name.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (an "Allow SDR Agent" profile permission) — access is granted by the permission set, not a profile setting.
Option B (access to an "SDR Agent object") — there is no such object.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.sales_agent_sdr_permissions.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: The support team at Coral Cloud Resorts needs to create a Flex prompt template that summarizes complex case histories for agent handoffs. The goal is to ensure summaries are concise and follow a specific three-part structure: Issue, Steps Taken, and Next Action. What should an Agentforce Specialist recommend to ensure consistent data output?
optionA: Use chain-of-thought reasoning.
optionB: Define the desired output structure with explicit headings in the instruction.
optionC: Use a prompt template-triggered flow to format responses.
explanation:
Defining the output structure with explicit headings in the instructions is the recommendation. Salesforce's prompt guidance is to use direct instructions for exactly the content you expect and to put them in a distinct instructions section, so naming the three parts — Issue, Steps Taken, Next Action — in the instructions produces consistent output.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (chain-of-thought reasoning) — improves reasoning on complex problems, not output layout.
Option C (a template-triggered flow to format responses) — those flows supply data into a template; they do not format the model's answer.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_best_practices.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_template_ingredients.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Pacific Distribution Co. is implementing a system to manage partner order support and inventory inquiries. The company needs to ensure that large documents are processed effectively to improve retrieval accuracy when agents respond to partner queries. Understanding how documents are broken down and indexed is crucial for this implementation. What is a key characteristic of the chunking process?
optionA: Chunking breaks large documents into smaller units called passages.
optionB: The chunking process returns entire documents to the large language model for processing.
optionC: Chunking strategies are interchangeable and do not affect the retrieval process.
explanation:
Chunking breaking large documents into smaller units, called passages, is the key characteristic. Salesforce's Chunk Data page says chunking breaks "your data into meaningful chunks" that Data 360 turns into vector embeddings, and its chunking strategies include semantic passage extraction.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (returns entire documents to the LLM) — the point of chunking is to return only the relevant pieces.
Option C (strategies are interchangeable) — Salesforce picks a strategy by content type because the choice changes what is retrieved.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_search_index_grounding.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=data.c360_a_search_index_supported_chunking_strategies.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers operates a customer self-service portal supported by an Agentforce Service Agent. The compliance team maintains a Salesforce Knowledge base of published product compliance guidelines, service terms, and regulatory procedures, updated regularly by subject matter experts. What is the most efficient approach to ensure the agent retrieves only current published content using semantic understanding of customer questions, and that outdated articles are never surfaced?
optionA: Build a subagent action using a Salesforce Flow to query the Knowledge articles data model object at runtime and return matching content to the agent, ensuring the agent always retrieves live article data directly from the Knowledge object.
optionB: Create an Agentforce Data Library connected to the Salesforce Knowledge base, filtered to published articles only, enabling the agent to ground responses using retrieval-augmented generation powered semantic retrieval that automatically reflects Knowledge updates without requiring agent reconfiguration.
optionC: Configure a custom retriever in Einstein Studio connected to a Data 360 search index, applying filters to restrict results to documents tagged as current.
explanation:
An Agentforce Data Library connected to Salesforce Knowledge, restricted to published articles, is the most efficient approach. Salesforce's Use Salesforce Knowledge page says "Only published articles are considered for the data library", and saving the library automatically creates the data streams, search index and retriever, so semantic retrieval follows Knowledge updates without reconfiguring the agent.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a flow querying the Knowledge DMO at runtime) — a structured query, not semantic retrieval, and a custom build.
Option C (a custom retriever filtering documents tagged "current") — relies on manual tagging, where Knowledge's publication state already does this.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_select_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_setup.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to ensure that its AI agent's responses consistently reflect the company's unique brand voice and specific quality standards beyond simple pass or fail checks. How should the Agentforce Specialist configure the Testing Center to evaluate this specific criteria?
optionA: Enable the Coherence quality evaluation
optionB: Use the default Response Evaluation metric
optionC: Create a custom evaluation using a large language model judge
explanation:
Creating a custom evaluation that uses an LLM judge is the way to measure brand voice. Salesforce's Create Custom Scorers says standard expectations "cover common test scenarios like topic matching and response coherence, but custom scorers create expectations tailored to your business requirements", and that scorers "use a prompt template to evaluate agent behavior automatically with an LLM".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Coherence) — checks for grammatical, conversational language, not a company's own voice.
Option B (the default Response Evaluation) — compares the response with an expected response; it does not score brand standards.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/testing-api-custom-scorers.html
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center_evaluations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: When using a prompt template, what should an Agentforce Specialist consider with their grounding data and chosen model?
optionA: Review the token limit in the Einstein Trust Layer.
optionB: Ensure queries used for grounding employ offset so the token limits of models are not exceeded.
optionC: Review the model limitation in Prompt Builder versus the grounding data size.
explanation:
Reviewing the model's limits in Prompt Builder against the size of the grounding data is the consideration. A template can hold up to 128,000 characters and pull in many merge fields, related lists and retrievers, while each model has its own token limits, listed in Salesforce's Large Language Model Limits — grounding that exceeds the chosen model's window is truncated or fails.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a token limit in the Einstein Trust Layer) — the Trust Layer masks, filters and audits; the limit belongs to the model.
Option B (use OFFSET in grounding queries) — pagination does not change how much grounding reaches the model in one prompt.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_limits.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.generative_ai_large_language_model_support.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: What should Universal Containers consider when deploying an Agentforce Service Agent with multiple topics and Agent Actions to production?
optionA: Deploy agent components without a test run in staging, relying on production data for reliable results. Sandbox configuration alone ensures seamless production deployment.
optionB: Ensure all dependencies are included, Apex classes meet 75% test coverage, and configuration settings are aligned with production. Plan for version management and post-deployment activation.
optionC: Deploy flows or Apex after agents, topics, and Agent Actions to avoid deployment failures and potential production agent issues requiring complete redeployment.
explanation:
Ensuring all dependencies are included, Apex meets 75% test coverage, settings align with production, and planning version management and post-deployment activation are the considerations. Salesforce's change-set article stresses including every interdependent component (actions, flows, Apex and agent metadata together); Apex needs at least 75% code coverage to deploy to production; and flows arrive inactive by default, so activation is a post-deployment step.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (skip staging and rely on production data) — deploying untested components straight to production is what staging exists to prevent.
Option C (deploy flows and Apex after the agent) — backwards; the agent's actions depend on them, so they must deploy first or together.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=005232697&language=en_US&type=1
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.apexcode.meta/apexcode/apex_code_coverage_intro.htm
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_distribute_deploy_active.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers wants to implement a solution in Salesforce with a custom UX that allows users to enter a sales order number. Subsequently, the system will invoke a custom prompt template to create and display a summary of the sales order header and sales order details. Which solution should an Agentforce Specialist implement to meet this requirement?
optionA: Create an autolaunched flow and invoke the prompt template using the standard "Prompt Template" flow action.
optionB: Create a template-triggered prompt flow and invoke the prompt template using the standard "Prompt Template" flow action.
optionC: Create a screen flow to collect the sales order number and invoke the prompt template using the standard "Prompt Template" flow action.
explanation:
A screen flow that collects the sales order number and calls the prompt template through the standard Prompt Template flow action is the solution. The screen flow supplies the custom UX for input and output, and the flow action runs the template and returns its generated text for the screen to display.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (an autolaunched flow) — has no screens, so it cannot collect the order number from the user.
Option B (a template-triggered prompt flow) — runs inside a template to supply grounding data; it does not provide a UI.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=platform.flow_ref_elements_actions_generate_prompt_response.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Specialist is testing an agent with Testing Center. The test results show that an agent correctly identifies the right subagent to handle an utterance, but it fails to select all necessary actions within that subagent. Which evaluation metric specifically identifies this failure?
optionA: Action Assertion
optionB: Response Evaluation
optionC: Subagent Assertion
explanation:
Action Assertion identifies the failure. Testing Center's Choose Evaluations page says the action assertion "checks that the agent selects the right actions and includes all of the expected actions based on the utterance", while the subagent assertion only checks that the right subagent was selected.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (Response Evaluation) — judges the final response against an expected response, not the actions chosen.
Option C (Subagent Assertion) — would pass here, since the subagent was correct.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.agent_testing_center_evaluations.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers has a requirement to provide a sales summary for its sales reps who are using Employee Agents, but they are not happy with the default answer. Which best practice should the Agentforce Specialist recommend?
optionA: Create a Record Summary custom prompt template.
optionB: Create a Knowledge Answer custom prompt template.
optionC: Update the standard record summary action.
explanation:
Creating a custom Record Summary prompt template is the best practice. Salesforce's Summarize Record action reference says the action "identifies active prompt templates of type Record Summary" and that "If multiple matching templates exist, custom (database) templates are prioritized over Salesforce-provided (file-based) templates", so a custom template for the object replaces the default answer.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (a Knowledge Answer template) — for answering questions from Knowledge, not summarizing records.
Option C (update the standard action) — standard actions are not edited; their behaviour is customized through templates.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_actions_ref_summarize_record.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.prompt_builder_override_standard_template.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: An Agentforce Specialist wants to troubleshoot their Agent's performance. Where should the Agentforce Specialist go to access all user interactions with the Agent, including Agent errors, incorrectly triggered actions, and incomplete plans?
optionA: Plan Canvas
optionB: Agent Settings
optionC: Event Logs
explanation:
Event logs are where to see all interactions, errors and action problems. Salesforce's Enable Enhanced Event Logs says "Event logs capture the events and user messages in an agent session to help you test and troubleshoot your agent", with columns flagging errors and dropped sessions, and with enhanced logs on, "user messages as well as agent messages and events".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (Plan Canvas) — shows how the agent reasoned on one test utterance in the builder, not every user interaction.
Option B (Agent Settings) — where the agent is configured, not where sessions are reviewed.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.copilot_setup_enhanced_event_logs.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: Universal Containers (UC) wants to enable its sales team to get insights into product and competitor names mentioned during calls. How should UC meet this requirement?
optionA: Enable Einstein Conversation Insights, connect a recording provider, assign permission sets, and customize insights with up to 25 products.
optionB: Enable Einstein Conversation Insights, assign permission sets, define recording managers, and customize insights with up to 50 competitor names.
optionC: Enable Einstein Conversation Insights, enable sales recording, assign permission sets, and customize insights with up to 50 products.
explanation:
Enabling Einstein Conversation Insights, connecting a recording provider, assigning permission sets and customizing insights for products is the path. Salesforce's Set Up Einstein Conversation Insights lists those steps — "Connect a recording provider, assign permission sets, and define insights" — after which calls are processed automatically and mentions of products and competitors surface as insights. (The per-insight number in the option is the exam's; the setup steps are what distinguish it.)
Why the other options are wrong:
Option B (define recording managers) — not a setup step; calls come from a connected recording provider.
Option C (enable sales recording) — likewise not the documented step; ECI needs a recording provider connected.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.call_coaching_setup.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=sales.eci_call_summaries.htm&language=en_US&type=5

question: A company's support agent is inconsistently executing a mandatory fraud check action before processing refunds. In some conversations the fraud check fires, but in others the agent skips directly to issuing the refund. Upon review, an Agentforce Specialist recommends placing the instruction guideline with run @actions.fraud_check followed by run @actions.process_refund. What is the effect of this configuration change?
optionA: The fraud-check action will be more strongly suggested to the large language model (LLM), but it may still be skipped if the LLM determines it is not relevant to the conversation.
optionB: The fraud-check action will execute after the large language model (LLM) check if it missed it in the process step execution, but the agent will lose its ability to use an empathetic tone.
optionC: The fraud-check action will be forced to execute before the refund action in every conversation, because procedural instructions provide deterministic control over the execution order.
explanation:
The fraud-check action being forced to run before the refund in every conversation, because procedural instructions give deterministic control over execution order, is the effect. Salesforce's Agent Script actions reference says that calling an action with run in the reasoning logic means "the action is run every time the subagent is run", and logic instructions "run deterministically every time", in the order written.
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (more strongly suggested but still skippable) — describes a tool in reasoning.actions, not a run in the logic.
Option B (runs only if the LLM missed it, at the cost of an empathetic tone) — run is unconditional, and prompt instructions still control tone.
References:
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-ref-actions.html
https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/ai/agentforce/guide/ascript-lang.html

question: After configuring and saving a Salesforce Agentforce Data Library (regardless of the data source), which components are automatically created and available in Data Cloud?
optionA: A data pipeline, an indexing engine, and a query processor
optionB: A data connector, an analytics dashboard, and a workflow rule
optionC: A data stream, a search index, and a retriever
explanation:
A data stream, a search index and a retriever are created automatically. Salesforce's Use Salesforce Knowledge page says "After you save your selections, data streams, a search index, and a retriever are created automatically and available to view or edit in Data 360", and the setup page says a library's source "is indexed on Data Cloud where a search index and retriever are automatically created".
Why the other options are wrong:
Option A (a pipeline, an indexing engine and a query processor) — generic terms, not the Data 360 components created.
Option B (a connector, an analytics dashboard and a workflow rule) — none is created by a data library.
References:
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_select_fields.htm&language=en_US&type=5
https://help.salesforce.com/s/articleView?id=ai.data_library_setup.htm&language=en_US&type=5
